}\n\n        body {\n          font-family: 'Segoe UI', Tahoma, Geneva, Verdana, sans-serif;\n          background: linear-gradient(135deg, #1fc66b 0%, #10552f 100%);\n          min-height: 100vh;\n center;\n          color: #2c3e50;\n          font-size: 2.5rem;\n          margin-bottom: 2rem;\n          text-shadow: 2px 2px 4px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1);\n        }\n\n        .search-container {\n linear-gradient(135deg, #1fc66b 0%, #10552f 100%);\n          color: white;\n          border: none;\n          border-radius: 50px;\n          cursor: pointer;\n          transition: all 0.3s ease;\n  }\n\n        #searchButton:active {\n          transform: translateY(0);\n        }\n\n        #results {\n          display: grid;\n          grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(350px, 1fr));\n          gap: 2rem;\n          margin-top: 2rem;\n        }\n\n        .recipe {\n          background: white;\n          border-radius: 15px;\n          padding: 1.5rem;\n          box-shadow: 0 8px 25px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1);\n          transition: all 0.3s ease;\n          border: 1px solid rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.05);\n          overflow: hidden;\n        }\n\n        .recipe:hover {\n          transform: translateY(-5px);\n          box-shadow: 0 15px 35px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.15);\n        }\n\n        .recipe h3 {\n          color: #2c3e50;\n          font-size: 1.4rem;\n          margin-bottom: 1rem;\n          line-height: 1.3;\n          font-weight: 600;\n        }\n\n        .recipe img {\n          width: 100%;\n          height: 200px;\n          object-fit: cover;\n          border-radius: 10px;\n          margin-bottom: 1rem;\n          transition: transform 0.3s ease;\n        }\n\n        .recipe:hover img {\n          transform: scale(1.05);\n        }\n\n        .nutrition-info {\n          display: grid;\n          grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr;\n          gap: 0.5rem;\n          margin-top: 1rem;\n        }\n\n        .recipe p {\n          margin: 0.3rem 0;\n          font-size: 0.95rem;\n          color: #555;\n          display: flex;\n          justify-content: space-between;\n          align-items: center;\n          padding: 0.5rem;\n          background: #f8f9fa;\n          border-radius: 8px;\n        }\n\n        .recipe p strong {\n          color: #2c3e50;\n          font-weight: 600;\n        }\n\n        .error {\n          color: #e74c3c;\n          text-align: center;\n          font-size: 1.1rem;\n          padding: 2rem;\n          background: rgba(231, 76, 60, 0.1);\n          border-radius: 10px;\n          border: 1px solid rgba(231, 76, 60, 0.2);\n        }\n\n        .loading {\n          text-align: center;\n          font-size: 1.1rem;\n          color: #667eea;\n          padding: 2rem;\n        }\n\n border-radius: 10px;\n          border: 1px solid rgba(127, 140, 141, 0.2);\n        }\n\n        /* Responsive design */\n        @media (max-width: 768px) {\n          body {\n            padding: 1rem;\n          }\n\n          .container {\n            padding: 1.5rem;\n            border-radius: 15px;\n          }\n\n          h1 {\n            font-size: 2rem;\n            margin-bottom: 1.5rem;\n          }\n\n          .search-container {\n            flex-direction: column;\n            gap: 1rem;\n          }\n\n          #searchInput, #searchButton {\n            padding: 0.8rem 1.2rem;\n            font-size: 1rem;\n          }\n\n          #results {\n            grid-template-columns: 1fr;\n            gap: 1.5rem;\n          }\n\n          .nutrition-info {\n            grid-template-columns: 1fr;\n          }\n        }\n\n        @media (max-width: 480px) {\n          .container {\n            padding: 1rem;\n          }\n\n          h1 {\n            font-size: 1.8rem;\n          }\n\n          .recipe {\n            padding: 1rem;\n          }\n        }\n      &lt;/style&gt;\n    &lt;/head&gt;\n    &lt;body&gt;\n    &lt;div class=\"container\"&gt;\n      &lt;h1&gt;Recipe Search&lt;/h1&gt;\n      &lt;div class=\"search-container\"&gt;\n        &lt;input type=\"text\" id=\"searchInput\" placeholder=\"Search for delicious recipes...\"&gt;\n        &lt;button id=\"searchButton\"&gt;Search&lt;/button&gt;\n      &lt;/div&gt;\n\n      &lt;div id=\"results\"&gt;&lt;/div&gt;\n    &lt;/div&gt;\n\n    &lt;script&gt;\n      const searchInput = document.getElementById('searchInput');\n      const searchButton = document.getElementById('searchButton');\n      const resultsDiv = document.getElementById('results');\n\n      searchButton.addEventListener('click', searchRecipes);\n\n      searchInput.addEventListener('keypress', function (e) {\n        if (e.key === 'Enter') {\n          searchRecipes();\n        }\n      });\n\n      function searchRecipes() {\n        const query = searchInput.value.trim();\n        if (!query) {\n          alert('Please enter a search term.');\n          return;\n        }\n        const apiKey = 'YOUR_API_KEY';  // &lt;-- Replace with your spoonacular API key\n        const apiUrl = &#96;https://api.spoonacular.com/recipes/complexSearch?query=${encodeURIComponent(query)}&amp;number=5&amp;addRecipeNutrition=true&amp;apiKey=${apiKey}&#96;;\n\n        resultsDiv.innerHTML = '&lt;p&gt;Searching for recipes...&lt;/p&gt;';\n\n        fetch(apiUrl)\n          .then(response =&gt; response.json())\n          .then(data =&gt; {\n            resultsDiv.innerHTML = '';\n            if (!data.results || data.results.length === 0) {\n              resultsDiv.innerHTML = '&lt;div class=\"no-results\"&gt;No recipes found. Try a different search term!&lt;/div&gt;';\n              return;\n            }\n            data.results.forEach(recipe =&gt; {\n              const title = recipe.title;\n              const image = recipe.image;\n              let calories = '', protein = '', fat = '', carbs = '';\n              if (recipe.nutrition &amp;&amp; recipe.nutrition.nutrients) {\n                const nutrients = recipe.nutrition.nutrients;\n                const calInfo = nutrients.find(n =&gt; n.name === 'Calories');\n                const proteinInfo = nutrients.find(n =&gt; n.name === 'Protein');\n                const fatInfo = nutrients.find(n =&gt; n.name === 'Fat');\n                const carbsInfo = nutrients.find(n =&gt; n.name === 'Carbohydrates');\n                if (calInfo) calories = Math.round(calInfo.amount) + ' ' + calInfo.unit;\n                if (proteinInfo) protein = Math.round(proteinInfo.amount) + ' ' + proteinInfo.unit;\n                if (fatInfo) fat = Math.round(fatInfo.amount) + ' ' + fatInfo.unit;\n                if (carbsInfo) carbs = Math.round(carbsInfo.amount) + ' ' + carbsInfo.unit;\n              }\n              const recipeDiv = document.createElement('div');\n              recipeDiv.className = 'recipe';\n              recipeDiv.innerHTML = &#96;\n            &lt;h3&gt;${title}&lt;/h3&gt;\n            &lt;img src=\"${image}\" alt=\"${title}\"&gt;\n            &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Calories:&lt;/strong&gt; ${calories}&lt;/p&gt;\n            &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Carbs:&lt;/strong&gt; ${carbs}&lt;/p&gt;\n            &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Protein:&lt;/strong&gt; ${protein}&lt;/p&gt;\n            &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Fat:&lt;/strong&gt; ${fat}&lt;/p&gt;\n          &#96;;\n              resultsDiv.appendChild(recipeDiv);\n            });\n          })\n          .catch(error =&gt; {\n            console.error('Error fetching recipes:', error);\n            resultsDiv.innerHTML = '&lt;div class=\"error\"&gt;Error fetching recipes. Please try again later.&lt;/div&gt;';\n          });\n      }\n    &lt;/script&gt;\n  &lt;/body&gt;\n&lt;/html&gt;\n        \n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nYou can download the full HTML demo also from the [github repo](https://github.com/ddsky/spoonacular-api-tutorials/blob/1e88809bae2c4c510fe563f0c867062463a4b0e6/spoonacular-recipe-search/spoonacular-recipe-search-full-code.html).\n\n👉 Now just replace&#96;\"YOUR_API_KEY\"&#96; with your actual key, save the file, and open it in your browser. You should be able to search for recipes and see results appear with images and nutrition info.\n\n## Conclusion\n\nCongratulations! 🎊 You've built a fully functional recipe search app using the Spoonacular API. In this process, you learned how to make API calls with fetch, handle JSON responses, and update the DOM with results. We kept things simple with vanilla JavaScript to help you understand the fundamentals.\n\nFrom here, you can enhance the app in many ways -- for example, add loading spinners, improve the layout with CSS, allow pressing \"Enter\" to trigger search, or even add more details like recipe summary or ingredients.\n\nUsing Spoonacular's rich API, you have access to a treasure trove of food data. We only scratched the surface by using the basic search with macro nutrients. Feel free to explore other endpoints (the API can get detailed recipe instructions, similar recipes, ingredient lists, and more as seen in their docs).\n\nHappy coding and happy cooking! 🍲👩‍💻👨‍💻\n\n## Image Classification\n\nThis article compares 7 online image recognition services in the context of food recognition. In particular, my goal was to find out which service is best suited to recognize and classify the dish you ordered in a restaurant based on a picture you took.\n\nThere are plenty of services out there, but I decided to compare the following as they are leaders in the field and have stable APIs:\n\n[Amazon Rekognition](https://aws.amazon.com/rekognition/)\n\nImage analysis by Amazon. They do not seem to have a pre-trained food model, so I used their generic tagger. Each classified image comes back with a number of tags and confidences.\n\n[Clarifai](https://www.clarifai.com/predict)\n\nAn image analysis service that also features a special [food model](https://www.clarifai.com/models/food-image-recognition-model-bd367be194cf45149e75f01d59f77ba7), which I used for testing.\n\n[Google Cloud Vision](https://cloud.google.com/vision)\n\nAn image analysis service by Google that also does not come with a pre-trained food model.\n\n[Imagga](https://imagga.com/solutions/categorization-api)\n\nAnother image analysis service without a pre-trained food model. I used their generic tagger.\n\n[Microsoft Computer Vision](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/services/cognitive-services/computer-vision/)\n\nAn image analysis service or (as they call it) \"cognitive service\" by Microsoft. No food model available.\n\n[Watson Visual Recognition](https://www.ibm.com/cloud/watson-visual-recognition)\n\nIBM Watson for image analysis by IBM. IBM also created a pre-trained [food-specific model](https://www.ibm.com/blogs/cloud-archive/2017/05/watson-learns-see-food-introducing-watson-visual-recognition-food-model/) that I was able to use in their API.\n\n[spoonacular](https://spoonacular.com/food-api)\n\nThe spoonacular food API offers a food-specific model specifically trained on our test dataset.\n\nOkay, now that we know our contenders, let's take a look at what dataset we're working with.\n\n### The 50-Class Food Dataset\n\nOur goal is to build/test a food dish recognizer. That is, we don't want to recognize single ingredients, such as an apple, milk, or a cup of mushrooms, but rather complex dishes that you would order in a restaurant.\n\nTo achieve this, we used the spoonacular food ontology to create a set of 518 dishes and gathered 2,781,306 images in total (over 417 GB in file size). The spoonacular food ontology is rather fine-grained, so many of the dish categories were a bit too specific (e.g. \"lemon cookies\"), so I reduced it down to 50 common classes with about 300 manually checked images per class.\n\nThe final dataset is 50 classes with a total of 15,742 images (4.4 GB in size).\n\nThe images are a mixture of high quality, professional photographs (showing the perfect execution of the dish, usually NOT taken in a real restaurant setting) and \"real world\" images taken by people that actually ordered and received that dish (like pictures taken from the spoonacular food journal). The differences between the two types are often extreme, so I found it to be valuable to have both types in the dataset.\n\nHave a look at the following example classes, \"cookies\", \"burger\", and \"pancakes\":\n\nNow, here is the full list of the 50 food categories with images (here in [plain text](https://spoonacular.com/food-api/docs#Image-Classification-Categories)):\n\n### Comparison of Image Classification Services\n\nNow that we know the dataset we're working with we can test the services with pictures from the dataset. These tests can only give us a rough idea of how well the service works because, as stated earlier, not all of them have a food-specific model. More importantly, they are trained on a completely different taxonomy, which means they might not even know what \"bibimbap\" is or what \"churros\" look like.\n\nThe goal of this article, however, is to find out which services are well suited for real-world dish recognition without training your own models (as dataset preparation is the really hard part). In this context, it is fair to compare them against an unknown set of images and see what they think the images are.\n\nI classified the same 50 images per class using each service for 2,500 classifications in total. The super long image below shows the top 5 tags/categories that each service assigned the images for each class. The percentage after the classified category is the percentage of images that received that particular tag. For example, Amazon Rekognition classified 98% of the \"agnolotti\" images as \"Food\". Good start.\n\nAdditionally, I bolded the category names which we should consider correct for the given images. Since the other taxonomies are not exactly the same as spoonacular's, we should still count \"doughnut\" as correct even if the spoonacular class is \"donut\".\n\nThe spoonacular column is just there for referenceâ€”since spoonacular's classifier was trained using the dataset, the category names always match and the percentage of matches is of course often higher.\n\nThe last row in the table shows how many classes in the top 5 can be considered correct. Aside from the expected 50/50 for spoonacular, we can see that the two services with special food-related classifiers, Clarifai and Watson, outperformed the other services dramatically.\n\nIn particular, the Watson food classifier seems to have been trained on a more fine-grained taxonomy. This is not surprising, since they say they have 2,000 tags, ranging from specific dishes to broader categories like \"sweet\" and \"delicacy\" as well. They even differentiate between \"barbecued wing\" and \"buffalo wing\"!\n\nTo give you an idea which tags/categories each service assigned to the provided images, here are the top 50 tags for each service (for all 2,500 classified images). You can also [download the raw data](https://spoonacular.com/application/frontend/downloads/visual-recognition-comparison-charts.xlsx) if you're interested in seeing it all.\n\n##### Top 50 Classes for Amazon Rekognition\n\nAmazon answered with 1,029 different tags, which is to be expected for a general classifier. The funniest tags were \"T-Rex\", \"dynamite\", and \"toilet\" :)\n\n##### Top 50 Classes for Clarifai\n\nClarifai answered with a total of 740 different food-specific tags (remember, they have a food-specific model). Looking at the tags with a low frequency we can see that they don't only use dishes in their model, but also have plain ingredients such as \"starfruit\", \"watercress\", and even spices like \"cumin\" in their model.\n\n##### Top 50 Classes for Google Cloud Vision\n\nGoogle only had a generic model, which shows in the poor results. They answered with a total of 1,831 distinct tags, most of them food-related and some controversial ones like \"shark fin soup\" and \"foie gras\" as well.\n\n##### Top 50 Classes for Imagga\n\nImagga answered with a total of 832 distinct tags from their generic model. While most of them were food related, I also got back \"concrete\", \"snake\", and \"winter\" at times.\n\n##### Top 50 Classes for Microsoft Cloud Vision\n\nMicrosoft Cognitive Services' generic model came back with at total of 1,070 distinct tags - most of them food related.\n\n##### Top 50 Classes for IBM Watson\n\nWatson returned 873 distinct food-related tags from the food model.\n\n##### spoonacular Confusion Matrix\n\nFor spoonacular, we were able to create an actual confusion matrix. The y-axis shows the tested classes and the x-axis the model's prediction. The diagonal (top left to bottom right) shows correct classifications.\n\nThe total accuracy of spoonacular's model is 90%. Most problematic seems to be \"baked apple\" with only 71% accuracy, while \"beer\" and \"burger\" are recognized with 100% accuracy - cheers to that!\n\n### Resources and Tools Used\n\nTo run all the tests I used the [Palladian Java Toolkit](https://palladian.ai/). Its wrappers for the cloud services Clarifai, Imagga, Amazon Rekognition, IBM Watson, Google Cloud Vision, and Microsoft Cloud Vision made evaluation much easiser.\n\nThanks to BjÃ¶rn Hempel for writing his bachelor thesis on this topic, which you can [read here](https://palladian.ai/publications/Bj%C3%B6rn%20Hempel%20-%20Investigation%20of%20strategies%20for%20image%20classi%EF%AC%81cation.pdf).\n\nIf you're interested in more detailed information you can download the [raw data (Excel)](https://spoonacular.com/application/frontend/downloads/visual-recognition-comparison-charts.xlsx).\n\n### Summary\n\nIf you want to reliably tag food-related images, you may want to use a service that comes with a pre-trained food model such as Clarifai, Watson, or spoonacular. If you have the time, knowledge, and resources, you can of course create your own dataset and create a custom model. Most online services allow for custom training models, but dataset creation is definitely not to be underestimated.\n\nAlso, if you want to play around with the spoonacular dish classifier, I built this [demo](https://spoonacular.com/food-api/image-analyzer-demo).\n\n## Diet Definitions\n\nEvery API endpoint asking for an&#96;diet&#96; parameter can be fed with any of these diets.\n\n#### Gluten Free\n\nEliminating gluten means avoiding wheat, barley, rye, and other gluten-containing grains and foods made from them (or that may have been cross contaminated).\n\n#### Ketogenic\n\nThe keto diet is based more on the ratio of fat, protein, and carbs in the diet rather than specific ingredients. Generally speaking, high fat, protein-rich foods are acceptable and high carbohydrate foods are not. The formula we use is 55-80% fat content, 15-35% protein content, and under 10% of carbohydrates.\n\n#### Vegetarian\n\nNo ingredients may contain meat or meat by-products, such as bones or gelatin.\n\n#### Lacto-Vegetarian\n\nAll ingredients must be vegetarian and none of the ingredients can be or contain egg.\n\n#### Ovo-Vegetarian\n\nAll ingredients must be vegetarian and none of the ingredients can be or contain dairy.\n\n#### Vegan\n\nNo ingredients may contain meat or meat by-products, such as bones or gelatin, nor may they contain eggs, dairy, or honey.\n\n#### Pescetarian\n\nEverything is allowed except meat and meat by-products - some pescetarians eat eggs and dairy, some do not.\n\n#### Paleo\n\nAllowed ingredients include meat (especially grass fed), fish, eggs, vegetables, some oils (e.g. coconut and olive oil), and in smaller quantities, fruit, nuts, and sweet potatoes. We also allow honey and maple syrup (popular in Paleo desserts, but strict Paleo followers may disagree). Ingredients not allowed include legumes (e.g. beans and lentils), grains, dairy, refined sugar, and processed foods.\n\n#### Primal\n\nVery similar to Paleo, except dairy is allowed - think raw and full fat milk, butter, ghee, etc.\n\n#### Low FODMAP\n\nFODMAP stands for \"fermentable oligo-, di-, mono-saccharides and polyols\". Our ontology knows which foods are considered high in these types of carbohydrates (e.g. legumes, wheat, and dairy products)\n\n#### Whole30\n\nAllowed ingredients include meat, fish/seafood, eggs, vegetables, fresh fruit, coconut oil, olive oil, small amounts of dried fruit and nuts/seeds. Ingredients not allowed include added sweeteners (natural and artificial, except small amounts of fruit juice), dairy (except clarified butter or ghee), alcohol, grains, legumes (except green beans, sugar snap peas, and snow peas), and food additives, such as carrageenan, MSG, and sulfites.\n\nSee also [the comparison of popular diets](https://spoonacular.com/academy/which-diet-is-best-for-me)\n\n## How to Write a Chatbot\n\nHere is an easy way how to make a chatbot like the [spoonacular chatbot](https://spoonacular.com/chatbot) with JavaScript in 10 minutes.\n\n- Optionally, if you want spoonacular support in your bot: Sign up for a [RapidAPI key](https://rapidapi.com/spoonacular/api/recipe-food-nutrition).\n- Follow the instructions in the readme file.\n- Check out this [JavaScript chatbot repository](https://github.com/ddsky/chatbot) on GitHub.\n\n## How to use the spoonacular MCP server for AI clients\n\nFirst install the MCP server, the instructions are easy to follow on the [spoonacular API MCP Github page](https://github.com/ddsky/spoonacular-mcp).\n\nNow get your API key ready and open your favorite MCP client. In this tutorial we'll use Claude Desktop. Open the App config:\n\nNow paste in the following snippet and replace&#96;your_api_key_here&#96; with your API key.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n{\n  \"mcp-servers\": {\n    \"spoonacular\": {\n      \"command\": \"spoonacular-mcp\",\n      \"env\": {\n        \"SPOONACULAR_API_KEY\": \"your_api_key_here\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nAnd that's it! You can now ask about news and if your AI client decides that the spoonacular API has a proper answer it will contact the API on your behalf. See the video below for an example conversation.\n\n#### spoonacular API MCP in action with Claude Desktop\n\n## Rate Limiting &amp; Quotas\n\nEach API plan comes with a daily quota of points. Every API call you make costs a certain amount of points. Usually, every request is\n\n1 point\n\nand\n\n0.01 points\n\nper result returned, but there are many exceptions. At the bottom of each endpoint description you will find information about the number of points required for that endpoint.\n\nWhen you are on the free plan and your daily quota is used up, the API will respond with the [error code 402](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/List_of_HTTP_status_codes#/402) and no more calls can be made until your quota resets.\n\nYou have complete control over your quota by looking at your console dashboard and checking the API response headers that appear with every answer from the API. These response headers are:\n\n- &#96;X-API-Quota-Left&#96;: The number of points left today (depends on your plan).\n- &#96;X-API-Quota-Used&#96;: The number of points used in total today. This number resets to zero at midnight UTC ([click here](https://time.is/UTC) to compare to your local time zone).\n- &#96;X-API-Quota-Request&#96;: The number of points used by the request.\n\n#### Rate Limiting\n\nThere is a limit of how many requests you can make per second. The limits depend on the plan you are on. If you try making more requests you will receive a [429 error](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/List_of_HTTP_status_codes#/429).\n\n- Chef: 20 requests per second\n- Culinarian: 10 requests per second\n- Cook: 5 requests per second\n- Starter: 120 requests in 1 minute\n- Free: 60 requests in 1 minute\n\n## Authentication\n\nTo use the API you need an API key. You can get a free one by simply [signing up here](https://spoonacular.com/food-api/console).\n\nOnce you have your API key, you have to put it in the request URL for every request you make like so ?apiKey=YOUR-API-KEY.\n\nAttention: Only the first query parameter is prefixed with a ? (question mark), all subsequent ones will be prefixed with a &amp; (ampersand). That is how URLs work and nothing related to our API. Here's a full example with two parameters&#96;apiKey&#96; and&#96;includeNutrition&#96;: [https://api.spoonacular.com/recipes/716429/information?apiKey=YOUR-API-KEY&amp;includeNutrition=true](https://api.spoonacular.com/recipes/716429/information?apiKey=YOUR-API-KEY&amp;includeNutrition=true).\n\nPlease further note that parameters are case sensitive, it is&#96;apiKey&#96; not&#96;apikey&#96;.\n\nAlternatively, you can put the API key in the request header as&#96;x-api-key&#96;."
}

Learn more about quotas.\n\n#### Need Help? Just ask!\n\nAsk AI\n\n## Search Recipes\n\nSearch through thousands of recipes using advanced filtering and ranking. NOTE: This method combines searching by query, by ingredients, and by nutrients into one endpoint.\n\nIf you are making a \"what's in your fridge?\" style app and require more filters than the Search Recipes by Ingredients endpoint allows, use the sort parameters max-used-ingredients or min-missing-ingredients with this endpoint instead.\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/recipes/complexSearch\n\n#### Headers\n\nResponse Headers:\n\n- &#96;Content-Type: application/json&#96;\n\n#### Parameters\n\n| Name | Type | Example | Description |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| &#96;query&#96; | string | pasta | The (natural language) recipe search query. |\n| &#96;cuisine&#96; | string | italian | The cuisine(s) of the recipes. One or more, comma separated (will be interpreted as 'OR'). See a full [list of supported cuisines](https://spoonacular.com/food-api/docs#Cuisines). |\n| &#96;excludeCuisine&#96; | string | greek | The cuisine(s) the recipes must not match. One or more, comma separated (will be interpreted as 'AND'). See a full [list of supported cuisines](https://spoonacular.com/food-api/docs#Cuisines). |\n| &#96;diet&#96; | string | vegetarian | The diet(s) for which the recipes must be suitable. You can specify multiple with comma meaning AND connection. You can specify multiple diets separated with a pipe | meaning OR connection. For example diet=gluten free,vegetarian means the recipes must be both, gluten free and vegetarian. If you specify diet=vegan|vegetarian, it means you want recipes that are vegan OR vegetarian. See a full [list of supported diets](https://spoonacular.com/food-api/docs#Diets). |\n| &#96;intolerances&#96; | string | gluten | A comma-separated list of intolerances. All recipes returned must not contain ingredients that are not suitable for people with the intolerances entered. See a full [list of supported intolerances](https://spoonacular.com/food-api/docs#Intolerances). |\n| &#96;equipment&#96; | string | pan | The equipment required. Multiple values will be interpreted as 'or'. For example, value could be \"blender, frying pan, bowl\".See a full [list of supported equipment](https://spoonacular.com/food-api/docs#Equipment). |\n| &#96;includeIngredients&#96; | string | tomato,cheese | A comma-separated list of ingredients that should/must be used in the recipes. |\n| &#96;excludeIngredients&#96; | string | eggs | A comma-separated list of ingredients or ingredient types that the recipes must not contain. |\n| &#96;type&#96; | string | main course | The type of recipe. See a full [list of supported meal types](https://spoonacular.com/food-api/docs#Meal-Types). |\n| &#96;instructionsRequired&#96; | boolean | true | Whether the recipes must have instructions. |\n| &#96;fillIngredients&#96; | boolean | false | Add information about the ingredients and whether they are used or missing in relation to the query. |\n| &#96;addRecipeInformation&#96; | boolean | false | If set to true, you get more information about the recipes returned. |\n| &#96;addRecipeInstructions&#96; | boolean | false | If set to true, you get analyzed instructions for each recipe returned. The addRecipeInformation parameter needs to be true for this to take effect. |\n| &#96;addRecipeNutrition&#96; | boolean | false | If set to true, you get nutritional information about each recipes returned. |\n| &#96;author&#96; | string | coffeebean | The username of the recipe author. |\n| &#96;tags&#96; | string | myCustomTag | User defined tags that have to match. The author param has to be set. |\n| &#96;recipeBoxId&#96; | number | 2468 | The id of the recipe box to which the search should be limited to. |\n| &#96;titleMatch&#96; | string | Crock Pot | Enter text that must be found in the title of the recipes. |\n| &#96;maxReadyTime&#96; | number | 20 | The maximum time in minutes it should take to prepare and cook the recipe. |\n| &#96;minServings&#96; | number | 1 | The minimum amount of servings the recipe is for. |\n| &#96;maxServings&#96; | number | 8 | The maximum amount of servings the recipe is for. |\n| &#96;ignorePantry&#96; | boolean | true | Whether to ignore typical pantry items, such as water, salt, flour, etc. |\n| &#96;sort&#96; | string | calories | The strategy to sort recipes by. See a full [list of supported sorting options](https://spoonacular.com/food-api/docs#Recipe-Sorting-Options). |\n| &#96;sortDirection&#96; | string | asc | The direction in which to sort. Bruschetta Style Pork &amp; Pasta\",\n            \"image\": \"https://img.spoonacular.com/recipes/715538-312x231.jpg\",\n            \"imageType\": \"jpg\",\n        }\n    ],\n    \"totalResults\": 86\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe API response will give you arrays of usedIngredients, missedIngredients, and unusedIngredients for each returned recipe. This diagram shows you what they mean:\n\n#### Quotas\n\nCalling this endpoint requires\n\n1 point\n\nand\n\n0.01 points\n\nper result returned. Since this endpoint combines the capabilities of four different endpoints into one, additional points may be required depending on the parameters you set. If&#96;fillIngredients&#96; is set to true,\n\n0.025 points\n\nwill be added per recipe returned. If a nutrient filter is set,\n\n1 point\n\nwill be added. If&#96;addRecipeInformation&#96; is set to true,\n\n0.025 points\n\nwill be added per recipe returned. If&#96;addRecipeInstructions&#96; is set to true,\n\n0.025 points\n\nwill be added per recipe returned. If&#96;addRecipeNutrition&#96; is set to true,\n\n0.025 points\n\nwill be added per recipe returned and&#96;addRecipeInformation&#96; will automatically be set to true as well. Learn more about quotas.\n\n#### Need Help? Just ask!\n\nAsk AI\n\n## Get Recipe Information\n\nUse a recipe id to get full information about a recipe, such as ingredients, nutrition, diet and allergen information, etc.\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/recipes/{id}/information\n\n#### Headers\n\nResponse Headers:\n\n- &#96;Content-Type: application/json&#96;\n\n#### Parameters\n\n| Name | Type | Example | Description |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| &#96;id&#96; | number | 716429 | The id of the recipe. |\n| &#96;includeNutrition&#96; | boolean | false | Include nutrition data in the recipe information. Nutrition data is per serving. If you want the nutrition data for the entire recipe, just multiply by the number of servings. |\n| &#96;addWinePairing&#96; | boolean | false | Add a wine pairing to the recipe. |\n| &#96;addTasteData&#96; | boolean | false | Add taste data to the recipe. |\n\nExample Request and Response\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/recipes/716429/information?includeNutrition=false\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n    \"id\": 716429,\n    \"title\": \"Pasta with Garlic, Scallions, Cauliflower &amp; Breadcrumbs\",\n    \"image\": \"https://img.spoonacular.com/recipes/716429-556x370.jpg\",\n    \"imageType\": \"jpg\",\n    \"servings\": 2,\n    \"readyInMinutes\": 45,\n This is equivalent to calling the Get Recipe Information endpoint multiple times, but faster.\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/recipes/informationBulk\n\n#### Headers\n\nResponse Headers:\n\n- &#96;Content-Type: application/json&#96;\n\n#### Parameters\n\n| Name | Type | Example | Description |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| &#96;ids&#96; | string | 715538,716429 | A comma-separated list of recipe ids. |\n| &#96;includeNutrition&#96; | boolean | false | Include nutrition data to the recipe information. Nutrition data is per serving. If you want the nutrition data for the entire recipe, just multiply by the number of servings. |\n\nExample Request and Response\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/recipes/informationBulk?ids=715538,716429\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n[\n    {/* recipe data as in Get Recipe Information endpoint */},\n    {/* recipe data as in Get Recipe Information endpoint */}\n]\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Quotas\n\nCalling this endpoint requires\n\n1 point\n\nfor the first recipe and\n\n0.5 points\n\nfor every additional recipe returned. Just ask!\n\nAsk AI\n\n## Get Similar Recipes\n\nFind recipes which are similar to the given one.\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/recipes/{id}/similar\n\n#### Headers\n\nResponse Headers:\n\n- &#96;Content-Type: application/json&#96;\n\n#### Parameters\n\n| Name | Type | Example | Description |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| &#96;id&#96; | number | 715538 | The id of the source recipe for which similar recipes should be found. |\n| &#96;number&#96; | number | 1 | The number of random recipes to be returned (between 1 and 100). |\n\nExample Request and Response\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/recipes/715538/similar\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n[\n    {\n        \"id\": 209128,\n        \"title\": \"Dinner Tonight: Grilled Romesco-Style Pork\",\n        \"imageType\": \"jpg\",\n        \"readyInMinutes\": 45,\n        \"servings\": 4,\n        \"sourceUrl\": \"http://www.seriouseats.com/recipes/2008/07/grilled-romesco-style-pork-salad-recipe.html\"\n    },\n    {\n        \"id\": 31868,\n        \"title\": \"Dinner Tonight: Chickpea Bruschetta\",\n        \"imageType\": \"jpg\",\n        \"readyInMinutes\": 45,\n        \"servings\": 2,\n        \"sourceUrl\": \"http://www.seriouseats.com/recipes/2009/06/dinner-tonight-chickpea-bruschetta-babbo-nyc-recipe.html\"\n    }\n]\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Quotas\n\nCalling this endpoint requires\n\n1 point\n\nand\n\n0.01 points\n\nper recipe returned. Learn more about quotas.\n\n#### Need Help? Just ask!\n\nAsk AI\n\n## Get Random Recipes\n\nFind random (popular) recipes. If you need to filter recipes by diet, nutrition etc. you might want to consider using the complex recipe search endpoint and set the&#96;sort&#96; request parameter to&#96;random&#96;.\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/recipes/random\n\n#### Headers\n\nResponse Headers:\n\n- &#96;Content-Type: application/json&#96;\n\n#### Parameters\n\n| Name | Type | Example | Description |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| &#96;includeNutrition&#96; | boolean | true | Whether to include nutritional information to returned recipes. |\n| &#96;include-tags&#96; | string | vegetarian, dessert | The tags (can be diets, meal types, cuisines, or intolerances) that the recipe must have. |\n| &#96;exclude-tags&#96; | string | dairy | The tags (can be diets, meal types, cuisines, or intolerances) that the recipe must NOT have. |\n| &#96;number&#96; | number | 1 | The number of random recipes to be returned (between 1 and 100). |\n\nExample Request and Response\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/recipes/random?number=1&amp;include-tags=vegetarian,dessert&amp;exclude-tags=quinoa\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n    \"recipes\":[\n        {/* recipe data as in Get Recipe Information endpoint */}\n    ]\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Quotas\n\nCalling this endpoint requires\n\n1 point\n\nand\n\n0.01 points\n\nper recipe returned and\n\n0.5 points\n\nper recipe returned if&#96;includeNutrition&#96; is set to true. Learn more about quotas.\n\n#### Need Help? Just ask!\n\nAsk AI\n\n## Taste by ID\n\nGet a recipe's taste. The tastes supported are sweet, salty, sour, bitter, savory, and fatty. These tastes are between 0 and 100 while the spiciness value is in scoville on an open scale of 0 and above.\n\nEvery ingredient has each of these values and it is weighted by how much they contribute to the recipe. Spiciness is taking the weight of the spicy ingredient and multiplying it with its scoville amount. Of course, taste is also very personal and it depends on how it is prepared so all of the values should only give you an indication of how the dish tastes.\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/recipes/{id}/tasteWidget.json\n\n#### Headers\n\nResponse Headers:\n\n- &#96;Content-Type: application/json&#96;\n\n#### Parameters\n\n| Name | Type | Example | Description |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| &#96;id&#96; | number | 69095 | The recipe id. |\n| &#96;normalize&#96; | boolean | false | Normalize to the strongest taste. |\n\nExample Request and Response\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/recipes/69095/tasteWidget.json\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n    \"sweetness\": 28.79,\n    \"saltiness\": 26.74,\n    \"sourness\": 6.22,\n    \"bitterness\": 12.38,\n    \"savoriness\": 11.8,\n    \"fattiness\": 100,\n    \"spiciness\": 0\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Quotas\n\nCalling this endpoint requires\n\n1 point\n\n. Just ask!\n\nAsk AI\n\n## Extract Recipe from Website\n\nThis endpoint lets you extract recipe data such as title, ingredients, and instructions from any properly formatted website.\n\nThe API can also watch and extract recipes from videos that you can typically find on Facebook Reels, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, Pinterest Pins, or TikTok Shorts. Since this requires much more compute resources extraction from videos is turned off by default. You can set&#96;extractFromVideo&#96; to&#96;true&#96; if you want to support these kinds of recipe links (be aware that this costs extra points and a longer response time).\n\nFurthermore, if you set&#96;includeNutrition&#96; to&#96;true&#96;, you will receive a full nutritional profile of the recipe - independent of whether the original source has any nutrition information. spoonacular will compute the nutrition itself.\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/recipes/extract\n\n#### Headers\n\nResponse Headers:\n\n- &#96;Content-Type: application/json&#96;\n\n#### Parameters\n\n| Name | Type | Example | Description |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| &#96;url&#96; | string | https://foodista.com/recipe/ZHK4KPB6/chocolate-crinkle-cookies | The URL of the recipe page. |\n| &#96;extractFromVideo&#96; | boolean | false | If true and the URL points to a video recipe, for example a tiktok, youtube, facebook reel, or instagram reel video the API tries to extract the recipe from the video. This might take up to 30 seconds. If the URL is NOT a video URL this won't have any effect. |\n| &#96;forceExtraction&#96; | boolean | true | If true, the extraction will be triggered whether we already know the recipe or not. Use this only if information is missing as this operation is slower. |\n| &#96;analyze&#96; | boolean | false | If true, the recipe will be analyzed and classified resolving in more data such as cuisines, dish types, and more. |\n| &#96;includeNutrition&#96; | boolean | false | Whether nutrition data should be added to correctly parsed ingredients. |\n| &#96;includeTaste&#96; | boolean | false | Whether taste data should be added to correctly parsed ingredients. |\n\nExample Request and Response\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/recipes/extract?url=https://foodista.com/recipe/ZHK4KPB6/chocolate-crinkle-cookies\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{/* recipe data as in Get Recipe Information endpoint */}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Quotas\n\nCalling this endpoint requires\n\n1 point\n\n. Additionally,\n\n+1 point\n\nif&#96;forceExtraction&#96; is set to true,\n\n+50 points\n\nif&#96;extractFromVideo&#96; is set to true and\n\n+1 point\n\nif&#96;analyze&#96; is set to true.. Learn more about quotas.\n\n#### Need Help? Just ask!\n\nAsk AI\n\n## Analyze a Recipe Search Query\n\nParse a recipe search query to find out its intention.\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/recipes/queries/analyze\n\n#### Headers\n\nResponse Headers:\n\n- &#96;Content-Type: application/json&#96;\n\n#### Parameters\n\n| Name | Type | Example | Description |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| &#96;q&#96; | string | salmon with fusilli and no nuts | The recipe search query. |\n\nExample Request and Response\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/recipes/queries/analyze?q=salmon+with+fusilli+and+no+nuts\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n    \"dishes\": [\n        {\n            \"image\": \"https://img.spoonacular.com/ingredients_100x100/salmon.png\",\n            \"name\": \"salmon\"\n        }\n    ],\n    \"ingredients\": [\n        {\n            \"image\": \"fusilli.jpg\",\n            \"include\": true,\n            \"name\": \"fusilli\"\n        },\n        {\n            \"image\": \"nuts-mixed.jpg\",\n            \"include\": false,\n            \"name\": \"nuts mixed\"\n        }\n    ],\n    \"cuisines\": [],\n    \"modifiers\": []\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Quotas\n\nCalling this endpoint requires\n\n1 point\n\n. Learn more about quotas.\n\n#### Need Help? Just ask!\n\nAsk AI\n\n## Convert Amounts\n\nConvert amounts like \"2 cups of flour to grams\".\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/recipes/convert\n\n#### Headers\n\nResponse Headers:\n\n- &#96;Content-Type: application/json&#96;\n\n#### Parameters\n\n| Name | Type | Example | Description |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| &#96;ingredientName&#96; | string | flour | The ingredient which you want to convert. |\n| &#96;sourceAmount&#96; | number | 2.5 | The amount from which you want to convert, e.g. the 2.5 in \"2.5 cups of flour to grams\". |\n| &#96;sourceUnit&#96; | string | cups | The unit from which you want to convert, e.g. the grams in \"2.5 cups of flour to grams\". You can also use \"piece\", e.g. \"3.4 oz tomatoes to piece\" |\n| &#96;targetUnit&#96; | string | grams | The unit to which you want to convert, e.g. the grams in \"2.5 cups of flour to grams\". You can also use \"piece\", e.g. \"3.4 oz tomatoes to piece\" |\n\nExample Request and Response\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/recipes/convert?ingredientName=flour&amp;sourceAmount=2.5&amp;sourceUnit=cups&amp;targetUnit=grams\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n    \"sourceAmount\": 2.5,\n    \"sourceUnit\": \"cups\",\n    \"targetAmount\": 312.5,\n    \"targetUnit\": \"grams\",\n    \"answer\": \"2.5 cups flour translates to 312.5 grams.\"\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Quotas\n\nCalling this endpoint requires\n\n1 point\n\n. Just ask!\n\nAsk AI\n\n## Compute Glycemic Load\n\nRetrieve the glycemic index for a list of ingredients and compute the individual and total glycemic load.\n\nPOST\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/food/ingredients/glycemicLoad\n\n#### Headers\n\nRequest Headers:\n\n- &#96;Content-Type: application/json&#96;\n\nResponse Headers:\n\n- &#96;Content-Type: application/json&#96;\n\n#### Parameters\n\n| Name | Type | Example | Description |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| &#96;(post body)&#96; | string | { \"ingredients\":[ \"1 kiwi\", \"2 cups rice\", \"2 glasses of water\" ] } | A json body. |\n| &#96;language&#96; | string | en | The input language, either \"en\" or \"de\". |\n\nExample Request\n\nPOST\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/food/ingredients/glycemicLoad\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n    \"ingredients\":[\n        \"1 kiwi\",\n        \"2 cups rice\",\n        \"2 glasses of water\"\n    ]\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nExample Response\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n    \"totalGlycemicLoad\": 183.64,\n    \"ingredients\": [\n        {\n            \"id\": 9148,\n            \"original\": \"1 kiwi\",\n            \"glycemicIndex\": 52.67,\n            \"glycemicLoad\": 5.59\n        },\n        {\n            \"id\": 20444,\n            \"original\": \"2 cups rice\",\n            \"glycemicIndex\": 61.19,\n            \"glycemicLoad\": 178.05\n        },\n        {\n            \"id\": 14412,\n            \"original\": \"2 glasses of water\",\n            \"glycemicIndex\": 0.0,\n            \"glycemicLoad\": 0.0\n        }\n    ]\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Quotas\n\nCalling this endpoint requires\n\n1 point\n\nand\n\n0.1 points\n\nper ingredient. Learn more about quotas.\n\n#### Need Help? Just ask!\n\nAsk AI\n\n## Autocomplete Ingredient Search\n\nAutocomplete the entry of an ingredient.\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/food/ingredients/autocomplete\n\n#### Headers\n\nResponse Headers:\n\n- &#96;Content-Type: application/json&#96;\n\n#### Parameters\n\n| Name | Type | Example | Description |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| &#96;query&#96; | string | appl | The partial or full ingredient name. |\n| &#96;number&#96; | number | 10 | The number of results to return (between 1 and 100). |\n| &#96;language&#96; | text | en | Language code, either \"en\" or \"de\". |\n| &#96;metaInformation&#96; | boolean | false | Whether to return more meta information about the ingredients. |\n| &#96;intolerances&#96; | string | egg | A comma-separated list of intolerances. All recipes returned must not contain ingredients that are not suitable for people with the intolerances entered. \"oz\",\n            \"cup\",\n            \"serving\",\n            \"tablespoon\"\n        ]\n    },\n    {\n        \"name\": \"apple juice\",\n        \"image\": \"apple-juice.jpg\",\n Just ask!\n\nAsk AI\n\n## Ingredient Search\n\nSearch for simple whole foods (e.g. fruits, vegetables, nuts, grains, meat, fish, dairy etc.).\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/food/ingredients/search\n\n#### Headers\n\nResponse Headers:\n\n- &#96;Content-Type: application/json&#96;\n\n#### Parameters\n\n| Name | Type | Example | Description |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| &#96;query&#96; | string | apple | The partial or full ingredient name. |\n| &#96;addChildren&#96; | boolean | true | Whether to add children of found foods. |\n| &#96;minProteinPercent&#96; | number | 10 | The minimum percentage of protein the food must have (between 0 and 100). |\n| &#96;maxProteinPercent&#96; | number | 90 | The maximum percentage of protein the food can have (between 0 and 100). |\n| &#96;minFatPercent&#96; | number | 10 | The minimum percentage of fat the food must have (between 0 and 100). |\n| &#96;maxFatPercent&#96; | number | 90 | The maximum percentage of fat the food can have (between 0 and 100). |\n| &#96;minCarbsPercent&#96; | number | 10 | The minimum percentage of carbs the food must have (between 0 and 100). |\n| &#96;maxCarbsPercent&#96; | number | 90 | The maximum percentage of carbs the food can have (between 0 and 100). |\n| &#96;metaInformation&#96; | boolean | false | Whether to return more meta information about the ingredients. |\n| &#96;intolerances&#96; | string | egg | A comma-separated list of intolerances. All recipes returned must not contain ingredients that are not suitable for people with the intolerances entered. See a full [list of supported intolerances](https://spoonacular.com/food-api/docs#Intolerances). |\n| &#96;sort&#96; | string | calories | The strategy to sort ingredients by. You can sort by any nutrient listed [here](https://spoonacular.com/food-api/docs#Recipe-Sorting-Options). |\n| &#96;sortDirection&#96; | string | asc | The direction in which to sort. Must be either 'asc' (ascending) or 'desc' (descending). |\n| &#96;language&#96; | text | en | Language code, either \"en\" or \"de\". |\n| &#96;offset&#96; | number | 0 | The number of results to skip (between 0 and 990). |\n| &#96;number&#96; | number | 10 | The number of expected results (between 1 and 100). |\n\nExample Request and Response\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/food/ingredients/search?query=banana&amp;number=2&amp;sort=calories&amp;sortDirection=desc\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n    \"results\": [\n        {\n            \"id\": 19400,\n            \"name\": \"banana chips\",\n            \"image\": \"banana-chips.jpg\"\n        },\n        {\n            \"id\": 93779,\n            \"name\": \"banana liqueur\",\n            \"image\": \"limoncello.jpg\"\n        }\n    ],\n    \"offset\": 0,\n    \"number\": 2,\n    \"totalResults\": 13\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Quotas\n\nCalling this endpoint requires\n\n1 point\n\nand\n\n0.01 points\n\nper result if&#96;metaInformation&#96; is set to true. Learn more about quotas.\n\n#### Need Help? Just ask!\n\nAsk AI\n\n## Get Ingredient Substitutes\n\nSearch for substitutes for a given ingredient.\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/food/ingredients/substitutes\n\n#### Headers\n\nResponse Headers:\n\n- &#96;Content-Type: application/json&#96;\n\n#### Parameters\n\n| Name | Type | Example | Description |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| &#96;ingredientName&#96; | string | butter | The name of the ingredient you want to replace. |\n\nExample Request and Response\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/food/ingredients/substitutes?ingredientName=butter\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n    \"ingredient\": \"butter\",\n    \"substitutes\": [\n        \"1 cup = 7/8 cup shortening and 1/2 tsp salt\",\n        \"1 cup = 7/8 cup vegetable oil + 1/2 tsp salt\",\n        \"1/2 cup = 1/4 cup buttermilk + 1/4 cup unsweetened applesauce\",\n        \"1 cup = 1 cup margarine\"\n    ],\n    \"message\": \"Found 4 substitutes for the ingredient.\"\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Quotas\n\nCalling this endpoint requires\n\n1 point\n\n. Learn more about quotas.\n\n#### Need Help? Just ask!\n\nAsk AI\n\n## Get Ingredient Substitutes by ID\n\nSearch for substitutes for a given ingredient.\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/food/ingredients/{id}/substitutes\n\n#### Headers\n\nResponse Headers:\n\n- &#96;Content-Type: application/json&#96;\n\n#### Parameters\n\n| Name | Type | Example | Description |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| &#96;id&#96; | number | 1001 | The id of the ingredient you want substitutes for. |\n\nExample Request and Response\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/food/ingredients/1001/substitutes\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n    \"ingredient\": \"butter\",\n    \"substitutes\": [\n        \"1 cup = 7/8 cup shortening and 1/2 tsp salt\",\n        \"1 cup = 7/8 cup vegetable oil + 1/2 tsp salt\",\n        \"1/2 cup = 1/4 cup buttermilk + 1/4 cup unsweetened applesauce\",\n        \"1 cup = 1 cup margarine\"\n    ],\n    \"message\": \"Found 4 substitutes for the ingredient.\"\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Quotas\n\nCalling this endpoint requires\n\n1 point\n\n. Learn more about quotas.\n\n#### Need Help? Just ask!\n\nAsk AI\n\n## Compute Ingredient Amount\n\nCompute the amount you need of a certain ingredient for a certain nutritional goal. For example, how much pineapple do you have to eat to get 10 grams of protein?\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/food/ingredients/{id}/amount\n\n#### Headers\n\nResponse Headers:\n\n- &#96;Content-Type: application/json&#96;\n\n#### Parameters\n\n| Name | Type | Example | Description |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| &#96;id&#96; | number | 9266 | The id of the ingredient you want the amount for. |\n| &#96;nutrient&#96; | string | protein | The target nutrient. See a [list of supported nutrients](https://spoonacular.com/food-api/docs#Nutrition). |\n| &#96;target&#96; | number | 2 | The target number of the given nutrient. |\n| &#96;unit&#96; | string | oz | The target unit. |\n\nExample Request and Response\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/food/ingredients/9266/amount?nutrient=protein&amp;target=10&amp;unit=oz\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n    \"amount\": 65.32,\n    \"unit\": \"oz\"\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Quotas\n\nCalling this endpoint requires\n\n1 point\n\n. Learn more about quotas.\n\n#### Need Help? Just ask!\n\nAsk AI\n\n## Ingredients Widget\n\nVisualize ingredients of a recipe. Learn more about quotas.\n\n#### Need Help? Just ask!\n\nAsk AI\n\n## Grocery Products Overview\n\nThe spoonacular grocery products API allows you to search through all products. You can find products by query (e.g. \"pizza\") and/or by macro-nutrients (e.g. &lt;500 calories).\n\nOnce you found a product, you can get a lot of detailed information about it such as nutrition, ingredients, cost, and where to find it in the supermarket.\n\nspoonacular analyzes every product and tries to retrieve meta information. This information is stored in&#96;badges&#96;.\n\nHere is a list of all possible badges a product can have:\n\n- sprouted_grain\n- multigrain\n- whole_wheat\n- whole_grain\n- lactose_free\n- non_alcoholic\n- sustainable\n- halal\n- kosher\n- organic\n- gmo_free\n- nitrate_free\n- soy_free\n- corn_free\n- sulfite_free\n- sugar_free\n- no_preservatives\n- hormone_free\n- no_additives\n- fair_trade\n- wild_caught\n- cage_free\n- free_range\n- pasture_raised\n- no_added_sugar\n- grass_fed\n- no_artificial_ingredients\n- no_artificial_flavors\n- no_artificial_colors\n- msg_free\n- paleo\n- gluten_free\n- dairy_free\n- pescetarian\n- vegan\n- nut_free\n- vegetarian\n- primal\n- peanut_free\n- grain_free\n- wheat_free\n- egg_free\n\n## Search Grocery Products\n\nSearch packaged food products, such as frozen pizza or Greek yogurt.\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/food/products/search\n\n#### Headers\n\nResponse Headers:\n\n- &#96;Content-Type: application/json&#96;\n\n#### Parameters\n\n| Name | Type | Example | Description |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| &#96;query&#96; | string | greek yogurt | The search query. |\n| &#96;minCalories&#96; | number | 50 | The minimum amount of calories the product must have per serving. |\n| &#96;maxCalories&#96; | number | 800 | The maximum amount of calories the product can have per serving. |\n| &#96;minCarbs&#96; | number | 10 | The minimum amount of carbohydrates in grams the product must have per serving. |\n| &#96;maxCarbs&#96; | number | 100 | The maximum amount of carbohydrates in grams the product can have per serving. |\n| &#96;minProtein&#96; | number | 10 | The minimum amount of protein in grams the product must have per serving. |\n| &#96;maxProtein&#96; | number | 100 | The maximum amount of protein in grams the product can have per serving. |\n| &#96;minFat&#96; | number | 1 | The minimum amount of fat in grams the product must have per serving. |\n| &#96;maxFat&#96; | number | 100 | The maximum amount of fat in grams the product can have per serving. |\n| &#96;addProductInformation&#96; | boolean | false | If set to true, you get more information about the products returned. |\n| &#96;offset&#96; | number | 0 | The number of results to skip (between 0 and 990). |\n| &#96;number&#96; | number | 10 | The number of expected results (between 1 and 100). |\n\nExample Request and Response\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/food/products/search?query=pizza&amp;number=2\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n    \"products\": [\n        {\n            \"id\": 192386,\n            \"title\": \"Pizza Buddy: Frozen Pizza Dough, 16 Oz\",\n            \"imageType\": \"jpg\"\n        },\n        {\n            \"id\": 27693,\n            \"title\": \"Uno Pizza\",\n            \"imageType\": \"jpg\"\n        }\n    ],\n    \"totalProducts\": 1258,\n    \"type\": \"product\",\n    \"offset\": 0,\n    \"number\": 2\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Quotas\n\nCalling this endpoint requires\n\n1 point\n\nand\n\n0.01 points\n\nper result returned. Since this endpoint combines the capabilities of four different endpoints into one, additional points may be required depending on the parameters you set. If&#96;addProductInformation&#96; is set to true,\n\n1 point\n\nwill be added per product returned. Learn more about quotas.\n\n#### Need Help? Just ask!\n\nAsk AI\n\n## Search Grocery Products by UPC\n\nGet information about a packaged food using its UPC.\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/food/products/upc/{upc}\n\n#### Headers\n\nResponse Headers:\n\n- &#96;Content-Type: application/json&#96;\n\n#### Parameters\n\n| Name | Type | Example | Description |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| &#96;upc&#96; | number | 041631000564 | The product's UPC. |\n\nExample Request and Response\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/food/products/upc/041631000564\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n    \"id\": 30004,\n    \"title\": \"Swan Flour\",\n    \"badges\": [\n        \"egg_free\",\n        \"wheat_free\",\n        \"grain_free\",\n        \"peanut_free\",\n        \"primal\",\n        \"vegetarian\",\n        \"nut_free\",\n        \"vegan\",\n        \"pescetarian\",\n        \"dairy_free\",\n        \"paleo\",\n        \"gluten_free\"\n    ],\n    \"importantBadges\": [\n        \"gluten_free\",\n        \"paleo\",\n        \"primal\",\n        \"wheat_free\",\n        \"grain_free\"\n    ],\n    \"breadcrumbs\": [\n        \"flour\"\n    ],\n    \"generatedText\": \"Swan Flour: This product is an awesome fit if you are searching for a healthy flour. Just ask!\n\nAsk AI\n\n## Search Custom Foods\n\nSearch custom foods in a user's account.\n\nRead more about working with the meal planner.\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/food/customFoods/search\n\n#### Headers\n\nResponse Headers:\n\n- &#96;Content-Type: application/json&#96;\n\n#### Parameters\n\n| Name | Type | Example | Description |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| &#96;query&#96; | string | brat | The search query. |\n| &#96;username&#96; | string | dsky | The username. |\n| &#96;hash&#96; | string | 4b5v4398573406 | The private hash for the username. |\n| &#96;offset&#96; | number | 0 | The number of results to skip (between 0 and 990). |\n| &#96;number&#96; | number | 10 | The number of expected results (between 1 and 100). |\n\nExample Request and Response\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/food/customFoods/search?query=brat&amp;number=2&amp;username=dsky&amp;hash=4b5v4398573406\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n    \"customFoods\": [\n        {\n            \"id\": 15,\n            \"title\": \"Max Cafe Curry Bratwurst\",\n            \"servings\": 1,\n            \"imageUrl\": \"https://img.spoonacular.com/ingredients_100x100/bratwurst.jpg\",\n            \"price\": 6.9\n        }\n    ],\n    \"type\": \"customFood\",\n    \"offset\": 0,\n    \"number\": 10\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Quotas\n\nCalling this endpoint requires\n\n1 point\n\nand\n\n0.01 points\n\nper custom food returned. Learn more about quotas.\n\n#### Need Help? Just ask!\n\nAsk AI\n\n## Add Custom Foods\n\nAdd custom foods to a user's account. This could be something as simple as \"1 banana\" or even mini recipes like \"1 toast with jam\".\n\nRead more about working with the meal planner.\n\nPOST\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/food/customFoods/add\n\n#### Headers\n\nResponse Headers:\n\n- &#96;Content-Type: application/json&#96;\n\n#### Parameters\n\n| Name | Type | Example | Description |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| &#96;(post body)&#96; | string | { \"title\": \"My little afternoon snack\", \"servings\": 2 } | The json representing the custom food. |\n| &#96;username&#96; | string | dsky | The username. |\n| &#96;hash&#96; | string | 4b5v4398573406 | The private hash for the username. |\n\nHere's the sample post request. The \"id\" should only be sent if you update an existing custom food for the user. Only \"title\" and \"servings\" is required, everything else is optional.\n\nThe response will be the custom food's id. If an image is available you can get it via https://img.spoonacular.com/custom-foods/#ID#-90x90.jpg where #ID# is the custom food's id.\n\nExample Request Body\n\nPOST\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/food/customFoods/add\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n    \"id\": 1,\n    \"title\": \"Chickpea Lunchbox\",\n    \"servings\": 1,\n    \"customFoodBoxId\": 123,\n    \"nutrition\": {\n        \"calories\": 300\n    },\n    \"meta\": {\"diets\":[\"vegan\",\"vegetarian\"],\"intolerances\":[\"sesame\",\"soy\"]},\n    \"imageUrl\": \"https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1543353071-c953d88f7033?q=80&amp;w=500&amp;auto=format&amp;fit=crop\"\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Quotas\n\nCalling this endpoint requires\n\n5 points\n\n. Learn more about quotas.\n\n#### Need Help? Just ask!\n\nAsk AI\n\n## Generate Meal Plan\n\nGenerate a meal plan with three meals per day (breakfast, lunch, and dinner).\n\nRead more about working with the meal planner.\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/mealplanner/generate\n\n#### Headers\n\nResponse Headers:\n\n- &#96;Content-Type: application/json&#96;\n\n#### Parameters\n\n| Name | Type | Example | Description |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| &#96;timeFrame&#96; | string | day | Either for one \"day\" or an entire \"week\". |\n| &#96;targetCalories&#96; | number | 2000 | What is the caloric target for one day? The meal plan generator will try to get as close as possible to that goal. |\n| &#96;diet&#96; | string | vegetarian | Enter a diet that the meal plan has to adhere to. See a full [list of supported diets](https://spoonacular.com/food-api/docs#Diets). |\n| &#96;exclude&#96; | string | shellfish, olives | A comma-separated list of allergens or ingredients that must be excluded. |\n\nExample Request and Response\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/mealplanner/generate?timeFrame=day\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n    \"meals\": [\n        {\n            \"id\": 655219,\n            \"title\": \"Peanut Butter And Chocolate Oatmeal\",\n            \"imageType\": \"jpg\",\n            \"readyInMinutes\": 45,\n            \"servings\": 1,\n            \"sourceUrl\": \"https://spoonacular.com/recipes/peanut-butter-and-chocolate-oatmeal-655219\"\n        },\n        {\n            \"id\": 649931,\n            \"title\": \"Lentil Salad With Vegetables\",\n            \"imageType\": \"jpg\",\n            \"readyInMinutes\": 45,\n            \"servings\": 4,\n            \"sourceUrl\": \"https://spoonacular.com/recipes/lentil-salad-with-vegetables-649931\"\n        },\n        {\n            \"id\": 632854,\n            \"title\": \"Asian Noodles\",\n            \"imageType\": \"jpg\",\n            \"readyInMinutes\": 45,\n            \"servings\": 4,\n            \"sourceUrl\": \"https://spoonacular.com/recipes/asian-noodles-632854\"\n        }\n    ],\n    \"nutrients\": {\n        \"calories\": 1735.81,\n        \"carbohydrates\": 235.17,\n        \"fat\": 69.22,\n        \"protein\": 55.43\n    }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Quotas\n\nCalling this endpoint requires\n\n1 point\n\n. Learn more about quotas.\n\n#### Need Help? Just ask!\n\nAsk AI\n\n## Get Meal Plan Week\n\nRetrieve a meal planned week for the given user. Just ask!\n\nAsk AI\n\n## Add to Meal Plan\n\nAdd an item to the user's meal plan.\n\nRead more about working with the meal planner.\n\nPOST\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/mealplanner/{username}/items\n\n#### Headers\n\nResponse Headers:\n\n- &#96;Content-Type: application/json&#96;\n\n#### Parameters\n\n| Name | Type | Example | Description |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| &#96;username&#96; | string | dsky | The username. |\n| &#96;hash&#96; | string | 4b5v4398573406 | The private hash for the username. |\n\nExample Request and Body\n\nPOST\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/mealplanner/dsky/items\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n    \"date\": 1589500800,\n    \"slot\": 1,\n    \"position\": 0,\n    \"type\": \"INGREDIENTS\",\n    \"value\": {\n        \"ingredients\": [\n            {\n                \"name\": \"1 banana\"\n            }\n        ]\n    }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe field&#96;date&#96; is the timestamp of the day the item should be added to.\n\nThe field&#96;slot&#96; is either 1, 2, or 3 for breakfast, lunch, or dinner respectively.\n\nThe field&#96;position&#96; is the order in the slot.\n\nThe field&#96;type&#96; is either INGREDIENTS for simple foods such as \"1 banana\", PRODUCT for a grocery product, MENU_ITEM for a menu item, RECIPE for a recipe, or CUSTOM_FOOD for custom food.\n\nThe field&#96;value&#96; is information about the item and the structure depends on what&#96;type&#96; is set to. The example above shows what it would look like for type ingredient. If the type is PRODUCT, MENU_ITEM, or RECIPE the value must contain the field&#96;servings&#96; and the&#96;id&#96; of the respective item.\n\nExample for adding a recipe with&#96;type&#96; RECIPE.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n    \"date\": 1589500800,\n    \"slot\": 1,\n    \"position\": 0,\n    \"type\": \"RECIPE\",\n    \"value\": {\n        \"id\": 296213,\n        \"servings\": 2,\n        \"title\": \"Spinach Salad with Roasted Vegetables and Spiced Chickpea\",\n        \"imageType\": \"jpg\",\n    }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nExample for adding a grocery product with&#96;type&#96; PRODUCT.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n    \"date\": 1589500800,\n    \"slot\": 1,\n    \"position\": 0,\n    \"type\": \"PRODUCT\",\n    \"value\": {\n        \"id\": 183433,\n        \"servings\": 1,\n        \"title\": \"Ahold Lasagna with Meat Sauce\",\n        \"imageType\": \"jpg\"\n    }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nExample for adding a menu item with&#96;type&#96; MENU_ITEM.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n    \"date\": 1589500800,\n    \"slot\": 1,\n    \"position\": 0,\n    \"type\": \"MENU_ITEM\",\n    \"value\": {\n        \"id\": 378557,\n        \"servings\": 1,\n        \"title\": \"Pizza 73 BBQ Steak Pizza, 9\",\n        \"imageType\": \"png\"\n    }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nExample for adding a custom food with&#96;type&#96; CUSTOM_FOOD.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n    \"date\": 1589500800,\n    \"slot\": 1,\n    \"position\": 0,\n    \"type\": \"CUSTOM_FOOD\",\n    \"value\": {\n        \"id\": 348,\n        \"servings\": 1,\n        \"title\": \"Aldi Spicy Cashews - 30g\",\n        \"image\": \"https://img.spoonacular.com/ingredients_100x100/cashews.jpg\"\n    }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nExample for adding simple foods with&#96;type&#96; INGREDIENTS. You can either just pass a name with amount and unit or pass a more complex object with amount, name, and unit in separate fields (recommended).\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n    \"date\": 1589500800,\n    \"slot\": 1,\n    \"position\": 0,\n    \"type\": \"INGREDIENTS\",\n    \"value\": {\n        \"ingredients\": [\n            {\n                \"name\": \"1 banana\"\n            },\n            {\n                \"name\": \"coffee\",\n                \"unit\": \"cup\",\n                \"amount\": \"1\",\n                \"image\": \"https://img.spoonacular.com/ingredients_100x100/brewed-coffee.jpg\"\n            },\n        ]\n    }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nAlternatively you can add all items of a meal plan template to a user's meal plan with one call. Just pass the&#96;mealPlanTemplateId&#96; and the&#96;startDate&#96; in your request. The user's meal plan will be filled with template items starting on startDate (day 1 of the specified meal plan template).\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n    \"mealPlanTemplateId\": 120,\n  \t\"startDate\": 1596575356,\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nYou can also add multiple items with one request. Just pass a JSON Array with multiple items. See below for an example.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n[\n    {\n        \"date\": 1589500800,\n        \"slot\": 1,\n        \"position\": 0,\n        \"type\": \"INGREDIENTS\",\n        \"value\": {\n            \"ingredients\": [\n                {\n                    \"name\": \"1 banana\"\n                },\n                {\n                    \"name\": \"coffee\",\n                    \"unit\": \"cup\",\n                    \"amount\": \"1\",\n                    \"image\": \"https://img.spoonacular.com/ingredients_100x100/brewed-coffee.jpg\"\n                },\n            ]\n        }\n    },\n    {\n        \"date\": 1589500800,\n        \"slot\": 2,\n        \"position\": 0,\n        \"type\": \"CUSTOM_FOOD\",\n        \"value\": {\n            \"id\": 348,\n            \"servings\": 1,\n            \"title\": \"Aldi Spicy Cashews - 30g\",\n            \"image\": \"https://img.spoonacular.com/ingredients_100x100/cashews.jpg\"\n        }\n    }\n]\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Quotas\n\nCalling this endpoint requires\n\n1 point\n\nand\n\n0.1 points\n\nper additional item added. Learn more about quotas.\n\n#### Need Help? Just ask!\n\nAsk AI\n\n## Clear Meal Plan Day\n\nDelete all planned items from the user's meal plan for a specific day.\n\nRead more about working with the meal planner.\n\nDELETE\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/mealplanner/{username}/day/{date}\n\n#### Headers\n\nResponse Headers:\n\n- &#96;Content-Type: application/json&#96;\n\n#### Parameters\n\n| Name | Type | Example | Description |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| &#96;username&#96; | string | dsky | The username. |\n| &#96;date&#96; | string | 2020-06-01 | The date in the format yyyy-mm-dd. |\n| &#96;hash&#96; | string | 4b5v4398573406 | The private hash for the username. |\n\nExample Request and Response\n\nDELETE\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/mealplanner/dsky/day/2020-06-01?hash=4b5v4398573406\n\n#### Quotas\n\nCalling this endpoint requires\n\n1 point\n\n. Learn more about quotas.\n\n#### Need Help? Just ask!\n\nAsk AI\n\n## Connect User\n\nIn order to call user-specific endpoints, you need to connect your app's users to spoonacular users.\n\nJust call this endpoint with your user's information and you will get back a username and hash that you must save on your side. In future requests that you make on this user's behalf you simply pass their username and hash alongside your API key.\n\nRead more about working with the meal planner.\n\nPOST\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/users/connect\n\n#### Headers\n\nResponse Headers:\n\n- &#96;Content-Type: application/json&#96;\n\n#### Parameters\n\n| Name | Type | Example | Description |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| &#96;(post body)&#96; | string | { \"username\": \"cool user\", } | A json body. |\n\nExample Request Body\n\nPOST\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/users/connect\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n    \"username\": \"your user's name\",\n    \"firstName\": \"your user's first name\",\n    \"lastName\": \"your user's last name\",\n    \"email\": \"your user's email\"\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe response will give you the corresponding spoonacular usernamem, the password with which the user can log in to spoonacular.com, and the hash. Save this information permanently on your end and connect it with your user.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n    \"username\": \"api_123_user\",\n    \"spoonacularPassword\": \"meadwith31grapejam\",\n    \"hash\": \"q572587bq2405724q05\"\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Quotas\n\nCalling this endpoint requires\n\n1 point\n\n. Just ask!\n\nAsk AI\n\n## Dish Pairing for Wine\n\nFind a dish that goes well with a given wine.\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/food/wine/dishes\n\n#### Headers\n\nResponse Headers:\n\n- &#96;Content-Type: application/json&#96;\n\n#### Parameters\n\n| Name | Type | Example | Description |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| &#96;wine&#96; | string | malbec | The type of wine that should be paired, e.g. \"merlot\", \"riesling\", or \"malbec\". |\n\nExample Request and Response\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/food/wine/dishes?wine=malbec\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n    \"pairings\": [\n        \"stew\",\n        \"steak\",\n        \"chili\",\n        \"burger\"\n    ],\n    \"text\": \"Malbec is a dry red wine which is bold and full bodied. It goes especially well with round steak, tri tip steak, steak, boneless pork chops, and pizza burger.\"\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Quotas\n\nCalling this endpoint requires\n\n1 point\n\n. Learn more about quotas.\n\n#### Need Help? Just ask!\n\nAsk AI\n\n## Wine Pairing\n\nFind a wine that goes well with a food. Food can be a dish name (\"steak\"), an ingredient name (\"salmon\"), or a cuisine (\"italian\").\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/food/wine/pairing\n\n#### Headers\n\nResponse Headers:\n\n- &#96;Content-Type: application/json&#96;\n\n#### Parameters\n\n| Name | Type | Example | Description |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| &#96;food&#96; | string | steak | The food to get a pairing for. This can be a dish (\"steak\"), an ingredient (\"salmon\"), or a cuisine (\"italian\"). |\n| &#96;maxPrice&#96; | number | 50 | The maximum price for the specific wine recommendation in USD. |\n\nExample Request and Response\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/food/wine/pairing?food=steak\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n    \"pairedWines\": [\n        \"merlot\",\n        \"cabernet sauvignon\",\n        \"pinot noir\"\n    ],\n    \"pairingText\": \"Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, and Pinot Noir are my top picks for Steak. Learn more about quotas.\n\n#### Need Help? Just ask!\n\nAsk AI\n\n## Detect Food in Text\n\nTake any text and find all mentions of food contained within it. This task is also called Named Entity Recognition (NER). In this case, the entities are foods. Either dishes, such as pizza or cheeseburger, or ingredients, such as cucumber or almonds.\n\nPOST\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/food/detect\n\n#### Headers\n\nRequest Headers:\n\n- &#96;Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded&#96;\n\nResponse Headers:\n\n- &#96;Content-Type: application/json&#96;\n\n#### Parameters\n\n| Name | Type | Example | Description |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| &#96;text&#96; | string | I like to eat delicious tacos. The only thing better is a cheeseburger with cheddar. But then again, pizza with pepperoni, mushrooms, and tomatoes is so good too! | The text in which food items, such as dish names and ingredients, should be detected in. |\n\nExample Request and Response\n\nPOST\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/food/detect\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n    \"annotations\": [\n        {\n            \"annotation\": \"cheeseburger\",\n            \"image\": \"https://spoonacular.com/menuItemImages/cheeseburger.jpg\",\n            \"tag\": \"dish\"\n        },\n        {\n            \"annotation\": \"mushrooms\",\n            \"image\": \"https://img.spoonacular.com/ingredients_100x100/mushrooms.png\",\n            \"tag\": \"ingredient\"\n        },\n        {\n            \"annotation\": \"pepperoni\",\n            \"image\": \"https://img.spoonacular.com/ingredients_100x100/pepperoni.png\",\n            \"tag\": \"ingredient\"\n        },\n        {\n            \"annotation\": \"tomatoes\",\n            \"image\": \"https://img.spoonacular.com/ingredients_100x100/tomato.png\",\n            \"tag\": \"ingredient\"\n        },\n        {\n            \"annotation\": \"cheddar\",\n            \"image\": \"https://img.spoonacular.com/ingredients_100x100/cheddar-cheese.png\",\n            \"tag\": \"ingredient\"\n        },\n        {\n            \"annotation\": \"tacos\",\n            \"image\": \"https://spoonacular.com/menuItemImages/taco-isolated.jpg\",\n            \"tag\": \"dish\"\n        },\n        {\n            \"annotation\": \"pizza\",\n            \"image\": \"https://spoonacular.com/menuItemImages/cheese-pizza.png\",\n            \"tag\": \"dish\"\n        }\n    ]\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Interactive Demo\n\nChange the text in the box and press \"Detect\". Please be sure to read the [YouTube Terms of Service](https://www.youtube.com/static?template=terms) before embedding videos into your site or app.\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/food/videos/search\n\n#### Headers\n\nResponse Headers:\n\n- &#96;Content-Type: application/json&#96;\n\n#### Parameters\n\n| Name | Type | Example | Description |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| &#96;query&#96; | string | chicken soup | The search query. |\n| &#96;type&#96; | string | main course | The type of the recipes. See a full [list of supported meal types](https://spoonacular.com/food-api/docs#Meal-Types). |\n| &#96;cuisine&#96; | string | italian | The cuisine(s) of the recipes. One or more, comma separated. See a full [list of supported cuisines](https://spoonacular.com/food-api/docs#Cuisines). |\n| &#96;diet&#96; | string | vegetarian | The diet for which the recipes must be suitable. See a full [list of supported diets](https://spoonacular.com/food-api/docs#Diets). |\n| &#96;includeIngredients&#96; | string | tomato,cheese | A comma-separated list of ingredients that the recipes should contain. |\n| &#96;excludeIngredients&#96; | string | eggs | A comma-separated list of ingredients or ingredient types that the recipes must not contain. |\n| &#96;minLength&#96; | number | 0 | Minimum video length in seconds. |\n| &#96;maxLength&#96; | number | 999 | Maximum video length in seconds. |\n| &#96;offset&#96; | number | 0 | The number of results to skip (between 0 and 900). |\n| &#96;number&#96; | number | 10 | The number of results to return (between 1 and 100). |\n\nExample Request and Response\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/food/videos/search?query=pasta&amp;number=2\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n    \"videos\": [\n        {\n            \"title\": \"8 One-Pot Pastas\",\n            \"length\": 370,\n            \"rating\": 0.985984219269103,\n            \"shortTitle\": \"8 One-Pot Pastas\",\n            \"thumbnail\": \"https://i.ytimg.com/vi/YTZGPCCB2FU/mqdefault.jpg\",\n            \"views\": 550467,\n            \"youTubeId\": \"YTZGPCCB2FU\"\n        },\n        {\n            \"title\": \"Macaroni salad - pasta salad recipes - healthy recipe channel - quick tasty recipe - cooking channel\",\n            \"length\": 333,\n            \"rating\": 1.0,\n            \"shortTitle\": \"Macaroni salad\",\n            \"thumbnail\": \"https://i.ytimg.com/vi/81bn4p8H3Kg/mqdefault.jpg\",\n            \"views\": 307,\n            \"youTubeId\": \"81bn4p8H3Kg\"\n        }\n    ],\n    \"totalResults\": 172\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Quotas\n\nCalling this endpoint requires\n\n1 point\n\nand\n\n0.01 points\n\nper video returned.
