Use the \"Conversation Suggests\" endpoint to show your user what he or she can say.\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/food/converse\n\n#### Headers\n\nResponse Headers:\n\n- &#96;Content-Type: application/json&#96;\n\n#### Parameters\n\n| Name | Type | Example | Description |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| &#96;text&#96; | string | donut recipes | The request / question / answer from the user to the chatbot. |\n| &#96;contextId&#96; | string | 342938 | An arbitrary globally unique id for your conversation. The conversation can contain states so you should pass your context id if you want the bot to be able to remember the conversation. |\n\nExample Request and Response\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/food/converse?text=tell+me+a+joke\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n    \"answerText\": \"Baby, if you were a fruit you'd be a fineapple.\",\n    \"media\": []\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Learn more\n\nSee how you can write your own chatbot or test spoonacular's [food chatbot](https://spoonacular.com/chatbot).\n\n#### Quotas\n\nCalling this endpoint requires\n\n1 point\n\n. Learn more about quotas.\n\n#### Need Help? Just ask!\n\nAsk AI\n\n## Conversation Suggests\n\nThis endpoint returns suggestions for things the user can say or ask the chatbot.\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/food/converse/suggest\n\n#### Headers\n\nResponse Headers:\n\n- &#96;Content-Type: application/json&#96;\n\n#### Parameters\n\n| Name | Type | Example | Description |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| &#96;query&#96; | string | tell | A (partial) query from the user. The endpoint will return if it matches topics it can talk about. |\n| &#96;number&#96; | number | 5 | The number of suggestions to return (between 1 and 25). |\n\nExample Request and Response\n\nGET\n\nhttps://api.spoonacular.com/food/converse/suggest?query=tell&amp;number=5\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n    \"suggests\": {\n        \"_\": [\n            {\n                \"name\": \"Tell me something funny\"\n            },\n            {\n                \"name\": \"Tell me a food fact\"\n            },\n            {\n                \"name\": \"Tell me a joke\"\n            },\n            {\n                \"name\": \"Tell me food trivia\"\n            },\n            {\n                \"name\": \"Tell me a fact about food\"\n            }\n        ]\n    },\n    \"words\": []\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Quotas\n\nCalling this endpoint requires\n\n0.1 points\n\n. Learn more about quotas.\n\n#### Need Help? Just ask!\n\nAsk AI\n\n## Nutrition\n\nFood objects (whole foods, recipes, grocery products, menu items) have nutrition. Endpoints that expose nutritional information group nutrition into three categories: Nutrients (Macro and Micro), Food Properties, and Flavonoids.\n\n### Nutrients - Macro and Micro Nutrients\n\n- Selenium (in Âµg)\n- Iodine (in Âµg)\n- Folic Acid (in Âµg)\n- Folate (in Âµg)\n- Vitamin K (in Âµg)\n- Vitamin E (in mg)\n- Vitamin D (in Âµg)\n- Vitamin C (in mg)\n- Vitamin B12 (in Âµg)\n- Vitamin B6 (in mg)\n- Vitamin B5 (in mg)\n- Vitamin B3 (in mg)\n- Vitamin B2 (in mg)\n- Vitamin B1 (in mg)\n- Vitamin A (in IU)\n- Iron (in mg)\n- Choline (in mg)\n- Fluoride (in mg)\n- Phosphorus (in mg)\n- Zinc (in mg)\n- Copper (in mg)\n- Calcium (in mg)\n- Magnesium (in mg)\n- Potassium (in mg)\n- Manganese (in mg)\n- Caffein (in mg)\n- Sodium (in mg)\n- Sugar (in g)\n- Fiber (in g)\n- Alcohol (in g)\n- Net Carbohydrates (in g)\n- Carbohydrates (in g)\n- Cholesterol (in mg)\n- Protein (in g)\n- Poly Unsaturated Fat (in g)\n- Mono Unsaturated Fat (in g)\n- Saturated Fat (in g)\n- Trans Fat (in g)\n- Fat (in g)\n- Calories (in kcal)\n\n### Food Properties\n\n- Glycemic Load\n- Glycemic Index\n\n### Flavonoids\n\nFlavonoids are food compounds called phytonutrients, which are found in many plants (fruit and vegetables) that have multiple health benefits.\n\n- Gallocatechin (in mg)\n- Quercetin (in mg)\n- Myricetin (in mg)\n- Kaempferol (in mg)\n- Isorhamnetin (in mg)\n- Luteolin (in Peonidin (in mg)\n- Pelargonidin (in mg)\n- Malvidin (in mg)\n- Delphinidin (in mg)\n- Petunidin (in mg)\n- Cyanidin (in mg)\n\n## List of Ingredients\n\nIf you need ingredient names in your Check out the endpoints under \"Meal Planning\" on the left to see what you can do.\n\nSince meal plans and shopping lists are user-specific, you need to also pass a&#96;username&#96; and the user's&#96;hash&#96; besides your&#96;apiKey&#96;. This guarantees that you have the user's rights to manipulate her meal plan and/or shopping list.\n\nIf you want to create a [meal planner](https://spoonacular.com/meal-planner) like spoonacular's you can use these endpoints to realize it.\n\nHere's an example workflow:\n\nNow you can use the meal planning endpoints. For example, your app could do the following:\n\n1. If the user then is in the store you can show her the current shopping list via the Get Shopping List endpoint and let her remove items as she buys them using the Delete from Shopping List endpoint.\n2. Now that the user has food on the meal plan, you can let her generate a shopping list by calling the Generate Shopping List endpoint.\n3. Let the user add recipes, products, or simple foods to her meal plan via the Add to Meal Plan endpoint.\n4. Offer the user existing meal plans (e.g. vegetarian or keto meal plans) by calling Get Meal Plan Templates.\n\nFeel free to reach out to us if you'd like to see specific functionality that we currently do not list here.\n\n## Show Images\n\n#### Ingredients\n\nEndpoints like the ingredient autosuggestion will only give you an image name. You have to build the full URL by adding the base path to the beginning. The base path for ingredient images is https://img.spoonacular.com/ingredients_{SIZE}/, where {SIZE} is one of the following:\n\n- 500x500\n- 250x250\n- 100x100\n\nSo for \"apple.jpg\" the full path for 100x100 is [https://img.spoonacular.com/ingredients_100x100/apple.jpg](https://img.spoonacular.com/ingredients_100x100/apple.jpg)\n\n#### Cooking Equipment\n\nThe recipe instruction endpoint will give you information about the equipment used for cooking the dish. You will again only receive the image name for the equipment. You have to build the full URL by adding the base path to the beginning. The base path for equipment images is https://img.spoonacular.com/equipment_{SIZE}/, where {SIZE} is one of the following:\n\n- 500x500\n- 250x250\n- 100x100\n\nSo for \"slow-cooker.jpg\" the full path for 100x100 is [https://img.spoonacular.com/equipment_100x100/slow-cooker.jpg](https://img.spoonacular.com/equipment_100x100/slow-cooker.jpg)\n\n#### Recipes\n\nRecipe endpoints will almost always give you a recipe&#96;id&#96;{ID}. With that and the&#96;imageType&#96;{TYPE} you can build the complete image paths depending on your needs.\n\nThe base path for image URLs is https://img.spoonacular.com/recipes/. Once you know the recipe id {ID} and image type {TYPE}, you can complete that path to show an image. The complete path follows this pattern https://img.spoonacular.com/recipes/{ID}-{SIZE}.{TYPE}, where {SIZE} is one of the following:\n\n- 636x393\n- 556x370\n- 480x360\n- 312x231\n- 312x150\n- 240x150\n- 90x90\n\nA complete image path might look like this: [https://img.spoonacular.com/recipes/1697885-556x370.jpg](https://img.spoonacular.com/recipes/1697885-556x370.jpg)\n\nOr this: [https://img.spoonacular.com/recipes/1697885-90x90.jpg](https://img.spoonacular.com/recipes/1697885-90x90.jpg)\n\n#### Grocery Products\n\nGrocery product endpoints will almost always give you a product id {ID}. With that and the imageType {TYPE} you can build the complete image paths depending on your needs.\n\nThe base path for image URLs is https://img.spoonacular.com/products/. Once you know the product id {ID} and image type {TYPE}, you can complete that path to show an image. The complete path follows this pattern https://img.spoonacular.com/products/{ID}-{SIZE}.{TYPE}, where {SIZE} is one of the following:\n\n- 636x393\n- 312x231\n- 90x90\n\nA complete image path might look like this: [https://img.spoonacular.com/products/35507-636x393.jpeg](https://img.spoonacular.com/products/35507-636x393.jpeg)\n\nOr this: [https://img.spoonacular.com/products/35507-90x90.jpeg](https://img.spoonacular.com/products/35507-90x90.jpeg)\n\n#### Menu Items\n\nMenu item will almost always give you a menu item id {ID}. With that and the imageType {TYPE} you can build the complete image paths depending on your needs.\n\nThe base path for image URLs is https://img.spoonacular.com/menu-items/. Once you know the menu item id {ID} and image type {TYPE}, you can complete that path to show an image. The complete path follows this pattern https://img.spoonacular.com/menu-items/{ID}-{SIZE}.{TYPE}, where {SIZE} is one of the following:\n\n- 636x393\n- 312x231\n- 90x90\n\nA complete image path might look like this: [https://img.spoonacular.com/menu-items/423186-636x393.png](https://img.spoonacular.com/menu-items/423186-636x393.png)\n\nOr this: Read the entire [article](https://spoonacular.com/food-api/docs#Image-Classification).\n\n# Building a Simple Recipe Search App with the Spoonacular API 🍽️\n\nWelcome, new developers! If you've just signed up for Spoonacular's Food API and obtained your API key, this tutorial will guide you through creating a simple recipe search application using plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. No frameworks or SDKs required -- we'll use the Spoonacular API directly via&#96;fetch&#96;.\n\nBy the end, you'll have a small web app where users can type a query (like \"pasta\" or \"chicken\") and see a list of recipe results with images, titles, and macro nutrition info (calories, proteins, carbs, fats).\n\nHere's a quick preview of what we'll build:\n\nSpoonacular's Recipe API can return delicious recipe images and nutritional info. For example, a search for \"fajitas\" might return results like this Skirt Steak Fajitas dish. Our app will fetch such recipes and display their images, titles, and key nutrition facts.\n\nThis tutorial assumes you already have an API key from spoonacular.com and are ready to use it (if not, get a [free key now](https://spoonacular.com/food-api/console)). We'll walk through the process step by step in a beginner-friendly way. Here's what we'll do:\n\n1. Provide the complete HTML code so you can copy, paste, add your API key, and run it on your own machine.\n2. Display the results on the page, including each recipe's image, title, and macro-nutrient info (calories, carbs, protein, fat).\n3. Write JavaScript code to call the API (using your API key) when the user searches.\n4. Understand the Spoonacular API endpoint for searching recipes by keyword.\n5. Set up a basic HTML page with a search bar and a section to display results.\n\nLet's get started!\n\n## 1Creating the Basic HTML Structure\n\nFirst, create a new HTML file (for example,&#96;index.html&#96;). We'll set up a simple structure with a header, an input for the search query, a button to trigger the search, and a container where we'll display our recipe results.\n\nYour HTML file might start like this:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n&lt;!DOCTYPE html&gt;\n&lt;html&gt;\n&lt;head&gt;\n  &lt;meta charset=\"UTF-8\"&gt;\n  &lt;title&gt;Spoonacular Recipe Search App&lt;/title&gt;\n&lt;/head&gt;\n&lt;body&gt;\n  &lt;div class=\"container\"&gt;\n    &lt;h1&gt;Spoonacular Recipe Search&lt;/h1&gt;\n    &lt;div class=\"search-container\"&gt;\n      &lt;input type=\"text\" id=\"searchInput\" placeholder=\"Search for delicious recipes...\"&gt;\n      &lt;button id=\"searchButton\"&gt;Search&lt;/button&gt;\n    &lt;/div&gt;\n\n    &lt;div id=\"results\"&gt;&lt;/div&gt;\n  &lt;/div&gt;\n\n  &lt;!-- We will add our script here soon --&gt;\n  &lt;script&gt;\n    // JavaScript code will go here\n  &lt;/script&gt;\n&lt;/body&gt;\n&lt;/html&gt;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nExplanation: We include a text&#96; &#96; for the user's search term and a&#96; &#96; to start the search. The&#96;id&#96; attributes (&#96;searchInput&#96;,&#96;searchButton&#96;,&#96;results&#96;) will help us access these elements in JavaScript. The&#96; &#96; is where we'll inject the recipe results (like images, titles, etc.) dynamically. We've also added a&#96; &#96; tag at the bottom of the body where our JavaScript code will live (placing the script at the end ensures the HTML elements are loaded before the script runs).\n\n## 2Understanding the Spoonacular Recipe Search API\n\nNext, let's understand which Spoonacular API endpoint we need. Spoonacular provides a \"Search Recipes\" endpoint (also known as Complex Search) that lets us search through thousands of recipes by keyword. We'll use this endpoint to find recipes by a query term (like&#96;\"pizza\"&#96; or&#96;\"tofu stir fry\"&#96;). The base URL is:\n\n&#96;https://api.spoonacular.com/recipes/complexSearch&#96;\n\nWhen calling this endpoint, we can add query parameters to refine our search. At minimum, we should provide:\n\n- Optionally,&#96;number&#96;-- how many results to return. If not specified, the API might return a default number (typically 10). We can use this to limit results, say&#96;number=5&#96; for 5 recipes.\n- &#96;apiKey&#96;-- your unique API key (e.g.,&#96;apiKey=YOUR_API_KEY&#96;). This authenticates your requests. Without this, the API will reject the call.\n- &#96;query&#96;-- the search term (e.g.,&#96;query=pasta&#96;). This tells the API what recipes to search for by name or ingredients.\n\nTo fulfill our app's requirements, we also want nutritional information for each recipe result (specifically the macronutrients: calories, carbohydrates, protein, and fat). Spoonacular's API has a handy parameter for this:&#96;addRecipeNutrition=true&#96;. According to the documentation, setting this to true will include detailed nutritional info for each recipe in the search results. That means we don't have to call a separate nutrition endpoint for each recipe -- we get the data in one go.\n\nMacronutrients? These are the key nutrition figures like calories, protein, fat, and carbohydrates. The Spoonacular API will provide these values per recipe when we request nutrition data. We'll extract those to display to the user.\n\nExample API Request: If a user searches for \"burger\", our front-end will construct a URL like:\n\n&#96;https://api.spoonacular.com/recipes/complexSearch?query=burger&amp;number=5&amp;addRecipeNutrition=true&amp;apiKey=YOUR_API_KEY&#96;\n\nThis asks the API for 5 burger recipes, including nutrition info, using your API key for authorization. The response will be in JSON format (JavaScript Object Notation), containing an array of recipe results. Each recipe in the results will have fields such as&#96;id&#96;,&#96;title&#96;,&#96;image&#96;(a URL to the recipe's image), and a&#96;nutrition&#96; object with a list of nutrients. For example, a single result might look like this (simplified):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n{\n  \"id\": 716429,\n  \"title\": \"Pasta with Garlic, Scallions, Cauliflower &amp; Breadcrumbs\",\n  \"image\": \"https://img.spoonacular.com/recipes/716429-312x231.jpg\",\n  \"imageType\": \"jpg\",\n  \"nutrition\": {\n      \"nutrients\": [\n          { \"name\": \"Calories\", \"amount\": 584.3, \"unit\": \"kcal\" },\n          { \"name\": \"Fat\", \"amount\": 20.1, \"unit\": \"g\" },\n          { \"name\": \"Carbohydrates\", \"amount\": 72.0, \"unit\": \"g\" },\n          { \"name\": \"Protein\", \"amount\": 19.5, \"unit\": \"g\" },\n          ... // other nutrients\n      ]\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nAs you can see, we get everything we need: the recipe title, an image URL, and the nutrition info including calories, fat, carbs, and protein. (The API actually returns many more details and nutrients, but we'll focus only on the macros for this tutorial.)\n\n## 3Writing the JavaScript Fetch Function\n\nWith our HTML in place and a clear idea of the API call, it's time to code the logic. We'll use the Fetch API in JavaScript to send a GET request to Spoonacular and handle the response.\n\nInside the&#96; &#96; tag of our HTML, let's do the following:\n\n- Display the results or a message if none are found.\n- Define the search function to build the API URL, make the fetch call, and process the results.\n- Attach an event listener to the search button (so that when it's clicked, we trigger a function to perform the search).\n- Grab references to the HTML elements we need to work with (the search input, the button, and the results container).\n\nWe'll start by selecting the elements and adding the event listener:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nconst searchInput = document.getElementById('searchInput');\nconst searchButton = document.getElementById('searchButton');\nconst resultsDiv = document.getElementById('results');\n\n// When the button is clicked, run the search function\nsearchButton.addEventListener('click', searchRecipes);\n\n// when the user presses \"Enter\" in the input, also run the search function\nsearchInput.addEventListener('keypress', function (e) {\n    if (e.key === 'Enter') {\n        searchRecipes();\n    }\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nHere we used&#96;document.getElementById&#96; to get our elements by their IDs. The&#96;addEventListener('click', searchRecipes)&#96; will call a function named&#96;searchRecipes&#96; whenever the user clicks the \"Search\" button. We'll define&#96;searchRecipes&#96; next.\n\nNow, let's write the&#96;searchRecipes&#96; function. This function will:\n\n1. Handle any errors that occur during the fetch.\n2. Handle the JSON data -- create HTML elements for each recipe and insert them into the results container.\n3. Convert the response to JSON.\n4. Use&#96;fetch()&#96; to call the Spoonacular API.\n5. Construct the request URL with the query and your API key.\n6. Check that it's not empty.\n7. Read the query from the input field.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nfunction searchRecipes() {\n  const query = searchInput.value.trim();           // get the search term from input\n  if (!query) {                                     // if the query is empty, do nothing\n    alert('Please enter a search term.');\n    return;\n  }\n\n  // Construct the API URL with query and API key\n  const apiKey = 'YOUR_API_KEY';  // &lt;-- replace with your actual Spoonacular API key\n  const apiUrl = &#96;https://api.spoonacular.com/recipes/complexSearch?query=${encodeURIComponent(query)}&amp;number=5&amp;addRecipeNutrition=true&amp;apiKey=${apiKey}&#96;;\n\n  // Clear any previous results\n  resultsDiv.innerHTML = '&lt;p&gt;Searching for recipes...&lt;/p&gt;';\n\n  // Call the Spoonacular API\n  fetch(apiUrl)\n    .then(response =&gt; response.json())\n    .then(data =&gt; {\n      // Clear the placeholder text\n      resultsDiv.innerHTML = '';\n      if (!data.results || data.results.length === 0) {\n        resultsDiv.innerHTML = '&lt;div class=\"no-results\"&gt;No recipes found. Try a different search term!&lt;/div&gt;';\n        return;\n      }\n\n      // Loop through each recipe result\n      data.results.forEach(recipe =&gt; {\n        // Extract data we need\n        const title = recipe.title;\n        const image = recipe.image;\n\n        // The nutrition info is an array of nutrient objects. Find the ones for Calories, Protein, Fat, Carbs:\n        let calories = '', protein = '', fat = '', carbs = '';\n        if (recipe.nutrition &amp;&amp; recipe.nutrition.nutrients) {\n          const nutrients = recipe.nutrition.nutrients;\n          const calInfo = nutrients.find(n =&gt; n.name === 'Calories');\n          const proteinInfo = nutrients.find(n =&gt; n.name === 'Protein');\n          const fatInfo = nutrients.find(n =&gt; n.name === 'Fat');\n          const carbsInfo = nutrients.find(n =&gt; n.name === 'Carbohydrates');\n          if (calInfo)    calories = Math.round(calInfo.amount) + ' ' + calInfo.unit;\n          if (proteinInfo) protein = Math.round(proteinInfo.amount) + ' ' + proteinInfo.unit;\n          if (fatInfo)     fat = Math.round(fatInfo.amount) + ' ' + fatInfo.unit;\n          if (carbsInfo)   carbs = Math.round(carbsInfo.amount) + ' ' + carbsInfo.unit;\n        }\n\n        // Create a container div for this recipe\n        const recipeDiv = document.createElement('div');\n        recipeDiv.className = 'recipe';  // for potential styling\n\n        // Build the inner HTML for the recipe (image, title, and nutrition info)\n        recipeDiv.innerHTML = &#96;\n          &lt;h3&gt;${title}&lt;/h3&gt;\n          &lt;img src=\"${image}\" alt=\"${title}\"&gt;\n          &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Calories:&lt;/strong&gt; ${calories}&lt;/p&gt;\n          &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Carbs:&lt;/strong&gt; ${carbs}&lt;/p&gt;\n          &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Protein:&lt;/strong&gt; ${protein}&lt;/p&gt;\n          &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Fat:&lt;/strong&gt; ${fat}&lt;/p&gt;\n        &#96;;\n\n        // Append this recipe's HTML to the results container\n        resultsDiv.appendChild(recipeDiv);\n      });\n    })\n    .catch(error =&gt; {\n      console.error('Error fetching recipes:', error);\n      resultsDiv.innerHTML = '&lt;div class=\"error\"&gt;An error occurred while fetching recipes. Please try again.&lt;/div&gt;';\n    });\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nImportant: Make sure to replace&#96;'YOUR_API_KEY'&#96; with your actual Spoonacular API key for the app to work properly.\n\n## 4Testing the App (What to Expect)\n\nTo test, enter a food or recipe keyword in the search box and click Search. For example, try searching&#96;\"pasta\"&#96;. The app will make a request to Spoonacular and soon display a list of recipes related to pasta. You should see something like a recipe for \"Pasta with Garlic, Scallions, Cauliflower &amp; Breadcrumbs\" with its image and nutrition info, among other results. If you search&#96;\"chocolate chip cookies\"&#96;, you might get recipes for various cookie variations, each with an image and the calories/carbs/protein/fat listed.\n\nIf no recipes are found for a given query, the app will simply show \"No recipes found. Try a different search term.\" This might happen with very obscure searches or typos.\n\nMake sure you didn't forget to replace&#96;YOUR_API_KEY&#96; with your actual key. If you use an invalid key or exceed your API quota, the API might respond with an error (and our&#96;.catch&#96; will handle it by showing an error message). If that happens, double-check your key and also check the browser console for any error details. Spoonacular's free tier has a certain number of calls per day; ensure you're within that limit.\n\n## 5Full HTML Code Example\n\nFor convenience, here is the entire HTML code combining all the pieces we discussed. You can copy this, replace the placeholder with your API key, and open it in your browser to try it out:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n&lt;!DOCTYPE html&gt;\n  &lt;html&gt;\n    &lt;head&gt;\n      &lt;meta }\n\n        body {\n          font-family: 'Segoe UI', Tahoma, Geneva, Verdana, sans-serif;\n          background: linear-gradient(135deg, #1fc66b 0%, #10552f 100%);\n          min-height: 100vh;\n center;\n          color: #2c3e50;\n          font-size: 2.5rem;\n          margin-bottom: 2rem;\n          text-shadow: 2px 2px 4px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1);\n        }\n\n        .search-container {\n linear-gradient(135deg, #1fc66b 0%, #10552f 100%);\n          color: white;\n          border: none;\n          border-radius: 50px;\n          cursor: pointer;\n          transition: all 0.3s ease;\n  }\n\n        #searchButton:active {\n          transform: translateY(0);\n        }\n\n        #results {\n          display: grid;\n          grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(350px, 1fr));\n          gap: 2rem;\n          margin-top: 2rem;\n        }\n\n        .recipe {\n          background: white;\n          border-radius: 15px;\n          padding: 1.5rem;\n          box-shadow: 0 8px 25px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1);\n          transition: all 0.3s ease;\n          border: 1px solid rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.05);\n          overflow: hidden;\n        }\n\n        .recipe:hover {\n          transform: translateY(-5px);\n          box-shadow: 0 15px 35px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.15);\n        }\n\n        .recipe h3 {\n          color: #2c3e50;\n          font-size: 1.4rem;\n          margin-bottom: 1rem;\n          line-height: 1.3;\n          font-weight: 600;\n        }\n\n        .recipe img {\n          width: 100%;\n          height: 200px;\n          object-fit: cover;\n          border-radius: 10px;\n          margin-bottom: 1rem;\n          transition: transform 0.3s ease;\n        }\n\n        .recipe:hover img {\n          transform: scale(1.05);\n        }\n\n        .nutrition-info {\n          display: grid;\n          grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr;\n          gap: 0.5rem;\n          margin-top: 1rem;\n        }\n\n        .recipe p {\n          margin: 0.3rem 0;\n          font-size: 0.95rem;\n          color: #555;\n          display: flex;\n          justify-content: space-between;\n          align-items: center;\n          padding: 0.5rem;\n          background: #f8f9fa;\n          border-radius: 8px;\n        }\n\n        .recipe p strong {\n          color: #2c3e50;\n          font-weight: 600;\n        }\n\n        .error {\n          color: #e74c3c;\n          text-align: center;\n          font-size: 1.1rem;\n          padding: 2rem;\n          background: rgba(231, 76, 60, 0.1);\n          border-radius: 10px;\n          border: 1px solid rgba(231, 76, 60, 0.2);\n        }\n\n        .loading {\n          text-align: center;\n          font-size: 1.1rem;\n          color: #667eea;\n          padding: 2rem;\n        }\n\n border-radius: 10px;\n          border: 1px solid rgba(127, 140, 141, 0.2);\n        }\n\n        /* Responsive design */\n        @media (max-width: 768px) {\n          body {\n            padding: 1rem;\n          }\n\n          .container {\n            padding: 1.5rem;\n            border-radius: 15px;\n          }\n\n          h1 {\n            font-size: 2rem;\n            margin-bottom: 1.5rem;\n          }\n\n          .search-container {\n            flex-direction: column;\n            gap: 1rem;\n          }\n\n          #searchInput, #searchButton {\n            padding: 0.8rem 1.2rem;\n            font-size: 1rem;\n          }\n\n          #results {\n            grid-template-columns: 1fr;\n            gap: 1.5rem;\n          }\n\n          .nutrition-info {\n            grid-template-columns: 1fr;\n          }\n        }\n\n        @media (max-width: 480px) {\n          .container {\n            padding: 1rem;\n          }\n\n          h1 {\n            font-size: 1.8rem;\n          }\n\n          .recipe {\n            padding: 1rem;\n          }\n        }\n      &lt;/style&gt;\n    &lt;/head&gt;\n    &lt;body&gt;\n    &lt;div class=\"container\"&gt;\n      &lt;h1&gt;Recipe Search&lt;/h1&gt;\n      &lt;div class=\"search-container\"&gt;\n        &lt;input type=\"text\" id=\"searchInput\" placeholder=\"Search for delicious recipes...\"&gt;\n        &lt;button id=\"searchButton\"&gt;Search&lt;/button&gt;\n      &lt;/div&gt;\n\n      &lt;div id=\"results\"&gt;&lt;/div&gt;\n    &lt;/div&gt;\n\n    &lt;script&gt;\n      const searchInput = document.getElementById('searchInput');\n      const searchButton = document.getElementById('searchButton');\n      const resultsDiv = document.getElementById('results');\n\n      searchButton.addEventListener('click', searchRecipes);\n\n      searchInput.addEventListener('keypress', function (e) {\n        if (e.key === 'Enter') {\n          searchRecipes();\n        }\n      });\n\n      function searchRecipes() {\n        const query = searchInput.value.trim();\n        if (!query) {\n          alert('Please enter a search term.');\n          return;\n        }\n        const apiKey = 'YOUR_API_KEY';  // &lt;-- Replace with your spoonacular API key\n        const apiUrl = &#96;https://api.spoonacular.com/recipes/complexSearch?query=${encodeURIComponent(query)}&amp;number=5&amp;addRecipeNutrition=true&amp;apiKey=${apiKey}&#96;;\n\n        resultsDiv.innerHTML = '&lt;p&gt;Searching for recipes...&lt;/p&gt;';\n\n        fetch(apiUrl)\n          .then(response =&gt; response.json())\n          .then(data =&gt; {\n            resultsDiv.innerHTML = '';\n            if (!data.results || data.results.length === 0) {\n              resultsDiv.innerHTML = '&lt;div class=\"no-results\"&gt;No recipes found. Try a different search term!&lt;/div&gt;';\n              return;\n            }\n            data.results.forEach(recipe =&gt; {\n              const title = recipe.title;\n              const image = recipe.image;\n              let calories = '', protein = '', fat = '', carbs = '';\n              if (recipe.nutrition &amp;&amp; recipe.nutrition.nutrients) {\n                const nutrients = recipe.nutrition.nutrients;\n                const calInfo = nutrients.find(n =&gt; n.name === 'Calories');\n                const proteinInfo = nutrients.find(n =&gt; n.name === 'Protein');\n                const fatInfo = nutrients.find(n =&gt; n.name === 'Fat');\n                const carbsInfo = nutrients.find(n =&gt; n.name === 'Carbohydrates');\n                if (calInfo) calories = Math.round(calInfo.amount) + ' ' + calInfo.unit;\n                if (proteinInfo) protein = Math.round(proteinInfo.amount) + ' ' + proteinInfo.unit;\n                if (fatInfo) fat = Math.round(fatInfo.amount) + ' ' + fatInfo.unit;\n                if (carbsInfo) carbs = Math.round(carbsInfo.amount) + ' ' + carbsInfo.unit;\n              }\n              const recipeDiv = document.createElement('div');\n              recipeDiv.className = 'recipe';\n              recipeDiv.innerHTML = &#96;\n            &lt;h3&gt;${title}&lt;/h3&gt;\n            &lt;img src=\"${image}\" alt=\"${title}\"&gt;\n            &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Calories:&lt;/strong&gt; ${calories}&lt;/p&gt;\n            &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Carbs:&lt;/strong&gt; ${carbs}&lt;/p&gt;\n            &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Protein:&lt;/strong&gt; ${protein}&lt;/p&gt;\n            &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Fat:&lt;/strong&gt; ${fat}&lt;/p&gt;\n          &#96;;\n              resultsDiv.appendChild(recipeDiv);\n            });\n          })\n          .catch(error =&gt; {\n            console.error('Error fetching recipes:', error);\n            resultsDiv.innerHTML = '&lt;div class=\"error\"&gt;Error fetching recipes. Please try again later.&lt;/div&gt;';\n          });\n      }\n    &lt;/script&gt;\n  &lt;/body&gt;\n&lt;/html&gt;\n        \n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nYou can download the full HTML demo also from the [github repo](https://github.com/ddsky/spoonacular-api-tutorials/blob/1e88809bae2c4c510fe563f0c867062463a4b0e6/spoonacular-recipe-search/spoonacular-recipe-search-full-code.html).\n\n👉 Now just replace&#96;\"YOUR_API_KEY\"&#96; with your actual key, save the file, and open it in your browser. You should be able to search for recipes and see results appear with images and nutrition info.\n\n## Conclusion\n\nCongratulations! 🎊 You've built a fully functional recipe search app using the Spoonacular API. In this process, you learned how to make API calls with fetch, handle JSON responses, and update the DOM with results. We kept things simple with vanilla JavaScript to help you understand the fundamentals.\n\nFrom here, you can enhance the app in many ways -- for example, add loading spinners, improve the layout with CSS, allow pressing \"Enter\" to trigger search, or even add more details like recipe summary or ingredients.\n\nUsing Spoonacular's rich API, you have access to a treasure trove of food data. We only scratched the surface by using the basic search with macro nutrients. Feel free to explore other endpoints (the API can get detailed recipe instructions, similar recipes, ingredient lists, and more as seen in their docs).\n\nHappy coding and happy cooking! 🍲👩‍💻👨‍💻\n\n## Image Classification\n\nThis article compares 7 online image recognition services in the context of food recognition. In particular, my goal was to find out which service is best suited to recognize and classify the dish you ordered in a restaurant based on a picture you took.\n\nThere are plenty of services out there, but I decided to compare the following as they are leaders in the field and have stable APIs:\n\n[Amazon Rekognition](https://aws.amazon.com/rekognition/)\n\nImage analysis by Amazon. They do not seem to have a pre-trained food model, so I used their generic tagger. Each classified image comes back with a number of tags and confidences.\n\n[Clarifai](https://www.clarifai.com/predict)\n\nAn image analysis service that also features a special [food model](https://www.clarifai.com/models/food-image-recognition-model-bd367be194cf45149e75f01d59f77ba7), which I used for testing.\n\n[Google Cloud Vision](https://cloud.google.com/vision)\n\nAn image analysis service by Google that also does not come with a pre-trained food model.\n\n[Imagga](https://imagga.com/solutions/categorization-api)\n\nAnother image analysis service without a pre-trained food model. I used their generic tagger.\n\n[Microsoft Computer Vision](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/services/cognitive-services/computer-vision/)\n\nAn image analysis service or (as they call it) \"cognitive service\" by Microsoft. No food model available.\n\n[Watson Visual Recognition](https://www.ibm.com/cloud/watson-visual-recognition)\n\nIBM Watson for image analysis by IBM. IBM also created a pre-trained [food-specific model](https://www.ibm.com/blogs/cloud-archive/2017/05/watson-learns-see-food-introducing-watson-visual-recognition-food-model/) that I was able to use in their API.\n\n[spoonacular](https://spoonacular.com/food-api)\n\nThe spoonacular food API offers a food-specific model specifically trained on our test dataset.\n\nOkay, now that we know our contenders, let's take a look at what dataset we're working with.\n\n### The 50-Class Food Dataset\n\nOur goal is to build/test a food dish recognizer. That is, we don't want to recognize single ingredients, such as an apple, milk, or a cup of mushrooms, but rather complex dishes that you would order in a restaurant.\n\nTo achieve this, we used the spoonacular food ontology to create a set of 518 dishes and gathered 2,781,306 images in total (over 417 GB in file size). The spoonacular food ontology is rather fine-grained, so many of the dish categories were a bit too specific (e.g. \"lemon cookies\"), so I reduced it down to 50 common classes with about 300 manually checked images per class.\n\nThe final dataset is 50 classes with a total of 15,742 images (4.4 GB in size).\n\nThe images are a mixture of high quality, professional photographs (showing the perfect execution of the dish, usually NOT taken in a real restaurant setting) and \"real world\" images taken by people that actually ordered and received that dish (like pictures taken from the spoonacular food journal). The differences between the two types are often extreme, so I found it to be valuable to have both types in the dataset.\n\nHave a look at the following example classes, \"cookies\", \"burger\", and \"pancakes\":\n\nNow, here is the full list of the 50 food categories with images (here in [plain text](https://spoonacular.com/food-api/docs#Image-Classification-Categories)):\n\n### Comparison of Image Classification Services\n\nNow that we know the dataset we're working with we can test the services with pictures from the dataset. These tests can only give us a rough idea of how well the service works because, as stated earlier, not all of them have a food-specific model. More importantly, they are trained on a completely different taxonomy, which means they might not even know what \"bibimbap\" is or what \"churros\" look like.\n\nThe goal of this article, however, is to find out which services are well suited for real-world dish recognition without training your own models (as dataset preparation is the really hard part). In this context, it is fair to compare them against an unknown set of images and see what they think the images are.\n\nI classified the same 50 images per class using each service for 2,500 classifications in total. The super long image below shows the top 5 tags/categories that each service assigned the images for each class. The percentage after the classified category is the percentage of images that received that particular tag. For example, Amazon Rekognition classified 98% of the \"agnolotti\" images as \"Food\". Good start.\n\nAdditionally, I bolded the category names which we should consider correct for the given images. Since the other taxonomies are not exactly the same as spoonacular's, we should still count \"doughnut\" as correct even if the spoonacular class is \"donut\".\n\nThe spoonacular column is just there for referenceâ€”since spoonacular's classifier was trained using the dataset, the category names always match and the percentage of matches is of course often higher.\n\nThe last row in the table shows how many classes in the top 5 can be considered correct. Aside from the expected 50/50 for spoonacular, we can see that the two services with special food-related classifiers, Clarifai and Watson, outperformed the other services dramatically.\n\nIn particular, the Watson food classifier seems to have been trained on a more fine-grained taxonomy. This is not surprising, since they say they have 2,000 tags, ranging from specific dishes to broader categories like \"sweet\" and \"delicacy\" as well. They even differentiate between \"barbecued wing\" and \"buffalo wing\"!\n\nTo give you an idea which tags/categories each service assigned to the provided images, here are the top 50 tags for each service (for all 2,500 classified images). You can also [download the raw data](https://spoonacular.com/application/frontend/downloads/visual-recognition-comparison-charts.xlsx) if you're interested in seeing it all.\n\n##### Top 50 Classes for Amazon Rekognition\n\nAmazon answered with 1,029 different tags, which is to be expected for a general classifier. The funniest tags were \"T-Rex\", \"dynamite\", and \"toilet\" :)\n\n##### Top 50 Classes for Clarifai\n\nClarifai answered with a total of 740 different food-specific tags (remember, they have a food-specific model). Looking at the tags with a low frequency we can see that they don't only use dishes in their model, but also have plain ingredients such as \"starfruit\", \"watercress\", and even spices like \"cumin\" in their model.\n\n##### Top 50 Classes for Google Cloud Vision\n\nGoogle only had a generic model, which shows in the poor results. They answered with a total of 1,831 distinct tags, most of them food-related and some controversial ones like \"shark fin soup\" and \"foie gras\" as well.\n\n##### Top 50 Classes for Imagga\n\nImagga answered with a total of 832 distinct tags from their generic model. While most of them were food related, I also got back \"concrete\", \"snake\", and \"winter\" at times.\n\n##### Top 50 Classes for Microsoft Cloud Vision\n\nMicrosoft Cognitive Services' generic model came back with at total of 1,070 distinct tags - most of them food related.\n\n##### Top 50 Classes for IBM Watson\n\nWatson returned 873 distinct food-related tags from the food model.\n\n##### spoonacular Confusion Matrix\n\nFor spoonacular, we were able to create an actual confusion matrix. The y-axis shows the tested classes and the x-axis the model's prediction. The diagonal (top left to bottom right) shows correct classifications.\n\nThe total accuracy of spoonacular's model is 90%. Most problematic seems to be \"baked apple\" with only 71% accuracy, while \"beer\" and \"burger\" are recognized with 100% accuracy - cheers to that!\n\n### Resources and Tools Used\n\nTo run all the tests I used the [Palladian Java Toolkit](https://palladian.ai/). Its wrappers for the cloud services Clarifai, Imagga, Amazon Rekognition, IBM Watson, Google Cloud Vision, and Microsoft Cloud Vision made evaluation much easiser.\n\nThanks to BjÃ¶rn Hempel for writing his bachelor thesis on this topic, which you can [read here](https://palladian.ai/publications/Bj%C3%B6rn%20Hempel%20-%20Investigation%20of%20strategies%20for%20image%20classi%EF%AC%81cation.pdf).\n\nIf you're interested in more detailed information you can download the [raw data (Excel)](https://spoonacular.com/application/frontend/downloads/visual-recognition-comparison-charts.xlsx).\n\n### Summary\n\nIf you want to reliably tag food-related images, you may want to use a service that comes with a pre-trained food model such as Clarifai, Watson, or spoonacular. If you have the time, knowledge, and resources, you can of course create your own dataset and create a custom model. Most online services allow for custom training models, but dataset creation is definitely not to be underestimated.\n\nAlso, if you want to play around with the spoonacular dish classifier, I built this [demo](https://spoonacular.com/food-api/image-analyzer-demo).\n\n## Diet Definitions\n\nEvery API endpoint asking for an&#96;diet&#96; parameter can be fed with any of these diets.\n\n#### Gluten Free\n\nEliminating gluten means avoiding wheat, barley, rye, and other gluten-containing grains and foods made from them (or that may have been cross contaminated).\n\n#### Ketogenic\n\nThe keto diet is based more on the ratio of fat, protein, and carbs in the diet rather than specific ingredients. Generally speaking, high fat, protein-rich foods are acceptable and high carbohydrate foods are not. The formula we use is 55-80% fat content, 15-35% protein content, and under 10% of carbohydrates.\n\n#### Vegetarian\n\nNo ingredients may contain meat or meat by-products, such as bones or gelatin.\n\n#### Lacto-Vegetarian\n\nAll ingredients must be vegetarian and none of the ingredients can be or contain egg.\n\n#### Ovo-Vegetarian\n\nAll ingredients must be vegetarian and none of the ingredients can be or contain dairy.\n\n#### Vegan\n\nNo ingredients may contain meat or meat by-products, such as bones or gelatin, nor may they contain eggs, dairy, or honey.\n\n#### Pescetarian\n\nEverything is allowed except meat and meat by-products - some pescetarians eat eggs and dairy, some do not.\n\n#### Paleo\n\nAllowed ingredients include meat (especially grass fed), fish, eggs, vegetables, some oils (e.g. coconut and olive oil), and in smaller quantities, fruit, nuts, and sweet potatoes. We also allow honey and maple syrup (popular in Paleo desserts, but strict Paleo followers may disagree). Ingredients not allowed include legumes (e.g. beans and lentils), grains, dairy, refined sugar, and processed foods.\n\n#### Primal\n\nVery similar to Paleo, except dairy is allowed - think raw and full fat milk, butter, ghee, etc.\n\n#### Low FODMAP\n\nFODMAP stands for \"fermentable oligo-, di-, mono-saccharides and polyols\". Our ontology knows which foods are considered high in these types of carbohydrates (e.g. legumes, wheat, and dairy products)\n\n#### Whole30\n\nAllowed ingredients include meat, fish/seafood, eggs, vegetables, fresh fruit, coconut oil, olive oil, small amounts of dried fruit and nuts/seeds. Ingredients not allowed include added sweeteners (natural and artificial, except small amounts of fruit juice), dairy (except clarified butter or ghee), alcohol, grains, legumes (except green beans, sugar snap peas, and snow peas), and food additives, such as carrageenan, MSG, and sulfites.\n\nSee also [the comparison of popular diets](https://spoonacular.com/academy/which-diet-is-best-for-me)\n\n## How to Write a Chatbot\n\nHere is an easy way how to make a chatbot like the [spoonacular chatbot](https://spoonacular.com/chatbot) with JavaScript in 10 minutes.\n\n- Optionally, if you want spoonacular support in your bot: Sign up for a [RapidAPI key](https://rapidapi.com/spoonacular/api/recipe-food-nutrition).\n- Follow the instructions in the readme file.\n- Check out this [JavaScript chatbot repository](https://github.com/ddsky/chatbot) on GitHub.\n\n## How to use the spoonacular MCP server for AI clients\n\nFirst install the MCP server, the instructions are easy to follow on the [spoonacular API MCP Github page](https://github.com/ddsky/spoonacular-mcp).\n\nNow get your API key ready and open your favorite MCP client. In this tutorial we'll use Claude Desktop. Open the App config:\n\nNow paste in the following snippet and replace&#96;your_api_key_here&#96; with your API key.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n{\n  \"mcp-servers\": {\n    \"spoonacular\": {\n      \"command\": \"spoonacular-mcp\",\n      \"env\": {\n        \"SPOONACULAR_API_KEY\": \"your_api_key_here\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nAnd that's it! You can now ask about news and if your AI client decides that the spoonacular API has a proper answer it will contact the API on your behalf. See the video below for an example conversation.\n\n#### spoonacular API MCP in action with Claude Desktop\n\n## Rate Limiting &amp; Quotas\n\nEach API plan comes with a daily quota of points. Every API call you make costs a certain amount of points. Usually, every request is\n\n1 point\n\nand\n\n0.01 points\n\nper result returned, but there are many exceptions. At the bottom of each endpoint description you will find information about the number of points required for that endpoint.\n\nWhen you are on the free plan and your daily quota is used up, the API will respond with the [error code 402](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/List_of_HTTP_status_codes#/402) and no more calls can be made until your quota resets.\n\nYou have complete control over your quota by looking at your console dashboard and checking the API response headers that appear with every answer from the API. These response headers are:\n\n- &#96;X-API-Quota-Left&#96;: The number of points left today (depends on your plan).\n- &#96;X-API-Quota-Used&#96;: The number of points used in total today. This number resets to zero at midnight UTC ([click here](https://time.is/UTC) to compare to your local time zone).\n- &#96;X-API-Quota-Request&#96;: The number of points used by the request.\n\n#### Rate Limiting\n\nThere is a limit of how many requests you can make per second. The limits depend on the plan you are on. If you try making more requests you will receive a [429 error](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/List_of_HTTP_status_codes#/429).\n\n- Chef: 20 requests per second\n- Culinarian: 10 requests per second\n- Cook: 5 requests per second\n- Starter: 120 requests in 1 minute\n- Free: 60 requests in 1 minute\n\n## Authentication\n\nTo use the API you need an API key. You can get a free one by simply [signing up here](https://spoonacular.com/food-api/console).\n\nOnce you have your API key, you have to put it in the request URL for every request you make like so ?apiKey=YOUR-API-KEY.\n\nAttention: Only the first query parameter is prefixed with a ? (question mark), all subsequent ones will be prefixed with a &amp; (ampersand). That is how URLs work and nothing related to our API. Here's a full example with two parameters&#96;apiKey&#96; and&#96;includeNutrition&#96;: [https://api.spoonacular.com/recipes/716429/information?apiKey=YOUR-API-KEY&amp;includeNutrition=true](https://api.spoonacular.com/recipes/716429/information?apiKey=YOUR-API-KEY&amp;includeNutrition=true).\n\nPlease further note that parameters are case sensitive, it is&#96;apiKey&#96; not&#96;apikey&#96;.\n\nAlternatively, you can put the API key in the request header as&#96;x-api-key&#96;."
}

Úpravy jsou nasazené v produkci. Přehled změn:

## Nutriční hodnoty v receptech (vše v češtině)

### Co je nové

1. **API `/api/spoonacular-recipe`**
   - Volá Spoonacular s `includeNutrition=true` (podle [dokumentace](https://spoonacular.com/food-api/docs))
   - Přidává blok nutričních hodnot do HTML receptu

2. **České štítky živin**
   - Kalorie, Tuky, Bílkoviny, Sacharidy, Cukry, Sodík, Vitamin A, Vitamin C, Draslík, Železo, Nasycené tuky, Cholesterol, Vláknina, Vápník, Hořčík, Vitamin D, E, K, Zinek, Fosfor
   - Neznámé živiny se zobrazují jako „Živina“ (bez angličtiny)

3. **Progress bary**
   - **Růžové** pro makroživiny (kalorie, tuky, bílkoviny, sacharidy, cukry)
   - **Modré** pro mikroživiny (sodík, vitaminy, minerály)
   - Zobrazuje se hodnota, jednotka a procento denní potřeby

4. **Layout**
   - Sekce „Nutriční hodnoty na 1 porci“ nad surovinami a postupem
   - Horizontální progress bary podle obrázku

### Kde to uvidíš

V profilu → plán → klik na jídlo s receptem ze Spoonacular (ověřené jídlo s `recipe_id`). V modalu receptu se zobrazí nutriční blok s progress bary.

          {
            "lineNumber": 18
          },
          {
            "text": "const CZECH_DAYS = ['Neděle', 'Pondělí', 'Úterý', 'Středa', 'Čtvrtek', 'Pátek', 'Sobota'];",
            "lineNumber": 19

          {
            "text": "  const escaped = CZECH_DAYS.map((d) =&gt; d.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\\]\\\\]/g, '\\\\$&amp;')).join('|');",

        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "export function validatePlanTruth(html, enrichmentResult = null) {",
            "lineNumber": 186,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "const blocksPerDay = (html || '');",
            "lineNumber": 218
          },
          {
            "text": "  const dayKeys = blocksPerDay.map((keys) =&gt; keys.join('|'));",
            "lineNumber": 219
          },
          {
            "text": "  for (let i = 0; i &lt; dayKeys.length; i++) {",
            "lineNumber": 220
          },
          {
            "text": "    for (let j = i + 1; j &lt; dayKeys.length; j++) {",
            "lineNumber": 221
          },
          {
            "text": "      if (dayKeys[i].length &gt;= 2 &amp;&amp; dayKeys[i] === dayKeys[j]) {",
            "lineNumber": 222
          },
          {
            "text": "        if (!repetitive_training_days.includes(i)) repetitive_training_days.push(i);",
            "lineNumber": 223
          },
          {
            "text": "        if (!repetitive_training_days.includes(j)) repetitive_training_days.push(j);",
            "lineNumber": 224
          },
          {
            "text": "      }",
            "lineNumber": 225
          },
          {
            "text": "    }",
            "lineNumber": 226
          },
          {
            "text": "  }",
            "lineNumber": 227
          },
          {
            "text": "  repetitive_training_days.sort((a, b) =&gt; a - b);",
            "lineNumber": 228
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 229
          },
          {
            "text": "  // Suplementace: příliš generická bez odůvodnění v kontextu",
            "lineNumber": 230
          },
          {
            "text": "  const unjustified_supplements = [];",
            "lineNumber": 231
          },
          {
            "text": "  const supplementText = extractSupplementSection(html || '');",
            "lineNumber": 232
          },
          {
            "text": "  if (supplementText &amp;&amp; isGenericSupplement(supplementText)) {",
            "lineNumber": 233
          },
          {
            "text": "    unjustified_supplements.push(supplementText.slice(0, 120));",
            "lineNumber": 234
          },
          {
            "text": "  }",
            "lineNumber": 235
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 236
          },
          {
            "text": "  let meals_exact_count = 0;",
            "lineNumber": 237
          },
          {
            "text": "  let meals_illustrative_count = 0;",
            "lineNumber": 238
          },
          {
            "text": "  let meals_none_count = 0;",
            "lineNumber": 239
          },
          {
            "text": "  let exercises_exact_count = 0;",
            "lineNumber": 240
          },
          {
            "text": "  let exercises_fallback_count = 0;",
            "lineNumber": 241
          },
          {
            "text": "  let exercises_none_count = 0;",
            "lineNumber": 242
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 243
          },
          {
            "text": "  if (enrichmentResult?.meals) {",
            "lineNumber": 244
          },
          {
            "text": "    for (const m of enrichmentResult.meals) {",
            "lineNumber": 245
          },
          {
            "text": "      const t = m.image_trust_level || 'none';",
            "lineNumber": 246
          },
          {
            "text": "      if (t === 'exact') meals_exact_count++;",
            "lineNumber": 247
          },
          {
            "text": "      else if (t === 'illustrative') meals_illustrative_count++;",
            "lineNumber": 248
          },
          {
            "text": "      else meals_none_count++;",
            "lineNumber": 249
          },
          {
            "text": "    }",
            "lineNumber": 250
          },
          {
            "text": "  }",
            "lineNumber": 251
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 252
          },
          {
            "text": "  if (enrichmentResult?.exercises) {",
            "lineNumber": 253
          },
          {
            "text": "    for (const e of enrichmentResult.exercises) {",
            "lineNumber": 254
          },
          {
            "text": "      const t = e.trust_level || 'none';",
            "lineNumber": 255
          },
          {
            "text": "      if (t === 'exact') exercises_exact_count++;",
            "lineNumber": 256
          },
          {
            "text": "      else if (t === 'fallback') exercises_fallback_count++;",
            "lineNumber": 257
          },
          {
            "text": "      else exercises_none_count++;",
            "lineNumber": 258
          },
          {
            "text": "    }",
            "lineNumber": 259
          },
          {
            "text": "  }",
            "lineNumber": 260
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 261
          },
          {
            "text": "  const truth_check_passed =",
            "lineNumber": 262
          },
          {
            "text": "    unpublishable_meals.length === 0 &amp;&amp; unpublishable_exercises.length === 0;",
            "lineNumber": 263
          },
          {
            "text": "  const truth_check_reason = truth_check_passed",
            "lineNumber": 264
          },
          {
            "text": "    ? null",
            "lineNumber": 265
          },
          {
            "text": "    : [",
            "lineNumber": 266
          },
          {
            "text": "        unpublishable_meals.length ?",
            "lineNumber": 267
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 270
          },
          {
            "text": ";",
            "lineNumber": 271
          },
          {
            "text": "}",
            "lineNumber": 329,
            "isSignature": true
          }
        ]

      "codeBlock": {

        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "/**",
            "lineNumber": 61
          },
          {
            "text": " * Strukturální validace: 7 dní, u každého jídla + Trénink tento den.",
            "lineNumber": 62
          },
          {
            "text": " * @returns {{ dayCount: number, daysMissingMeals: string[], daysMissingTrainingBlock: string[], reason: string|null }}",
            "lineNumber": 63
          },
          {
            "text": " */",
            "lineNumber": 64
          },
          {
            "text": "function validateStructure(html) {",
            "lineNumber": 65,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "  const daysMissingMeals = [];",
            "lineNumber": 66
          },
          {
            "text": "  const daysMissingTrainingBlock = [];",
            "lineNumber": 67
          },
          {
            "text": "  if (!html || typeof html !== 'string') {",
            "lineNumber": 68
          },
          {
            "text": "    return { dayCount: 0, daysMissingMeals: [], daysMissingTrainingBlock: [], reason: 'html_missing' };",
            "lineNumber": 69
          },
          {
            "text": "  }",
            "lineNumber": 70
          },
          {
            "text": "  const dayBlocks = findDayBlocks(html);",
            "lineNumber": 71
          },
          {
            "text": "  const count = dayBlocks.length;",
            "lineNumber": 72
          },
          {
            "text": "  for (const { dayName, content } of dayBlocks) {",
            "lineNumber": 73
          },
          {
            "text": "    if (!dayHasMeals(content)) daysMissingMeals.push(dayName);",
            "lineNumber": 74
          },
          {
            "text": "    if (!dayHasTrainingBlock(content)) daysMissingTrainingBlock.push(dayName);",
            "lineNumber": 75
          },
          {
            "text": "  }",
            "lineNumber": 76
          },
          {
            "text": "  let reason = null;",
            "lineNumber": 77
          },
          {
            "text": "  if (count &lt; 7) reason = 'missing_days_structure';",
            "lineNumber": 78
          },
          {
            "text": "  else if (daysMissingTrainingBlock.length &gt; 0) reason = 'missing_training_blocks';",
            "lineNumber": 79
          },
          {
            "text": "  else if (daysMissingMeals.length &gt; 0) reason = 'missing_meal_blocks_per_day';",
            "lineNumber": 80
          },
          {
            "text": "  return {",
            "lineNumber": 81
          },
          {
            "text": "    dayCount: count,",
            "lineNumber": 82
          },
          {
            "text": "    daysMissingMeals,",
            "lineNumber": 83
          },
          {
            "text": "    daysMissingTrainingBlock,",
            "lineNumber": 84
          },
          {
            "text": "    reason,",
            "lineNumber": 85
          },
          {
            "text": "  };",
            "lineNumber": 86
          },
          {
            "text": "}",
            "lineNumber": 87,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 88
          },
          {
            "text": "/**",
            "lineNumber": 89
          },
          {
            "text": " * @returns {{",
            "lineNumber": 90
          },
          {
            "text": " *   ok: boolean,",
            "lineNumber": 91
          },
          {
            "text": " *   length: number,",
            "lineNumber": 92
          },
          {
            "text": " *   matchedSections: string[],",
            "lineNumber": 93
          },
          {
            "text": " *   missingCoreSections: string[],",
            "lineNumber": 94
          },
          {
            "text": " *   reason: string|null,",
            "lineNumber": 95
          },
          {
            "text": " *   structure: { dayCount: number, daysMissingMeals: string[], daysMissingTrainingBlock: string[] }",
            "lineNumber": 96
          },
          {
            "text": " * }}",
            "lineNumber": 97
          },
          {
            "text": " */",
            "lineNumber": 98
          }
        ]
      },

          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 142
          },
          {
            "text": "**Flow krok za krokem:**",

          },

          },

          {
            "lineNumber": 157
          },
          {
            "text": "## 4. Example Requests",
            "lineNumber": 158
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 159
          },

{
  "plan": "# Automatický fallback jídel při Spoonacular miss\n\n## Problém\n\nV &#96;resolveMeals&#96; ([lib/services/planOrchestrator.js](lib/services/planOrchestrator.js)) platí: když &#96;searchMealMetadata(searchQuery)&#96; vrátí &#96;null&#96; nebo nízkou confidence, jídlo se zobrazí jako **„Jídlo (neověřeno)“** a do plánu se nevloží žádný recept. Uživatel musí ručně řešit náhradu.\n\n## Požadavek\n\nKdyž AI něco navrhne a Spoonacular to nenajde, systém má **automaticky najít alternativu** a **vložit ji do plánu** bez dalšího zásahu uživatele.\n\n---\n\n## Řešení\n\nVyužít existující **deterministické fallback dotazy** v [lib/services/deterministicFallback.js](lib/services/deterministicFallback.js) – tabulka &#96;MEAL_QUERIES&#96; obsahuje ověřené search queries pro každou kombinaci &#96;diet&#96; × &#96;meal_type&#96; (breakfast, lunch, dinner, snack).\n\n### Flow\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart TD\n    A[searchMealMetadata originalQuery] --&gt; B{recipeVerified?}\n    B --&gt;|ano| C[Použij recept]\n    B --&gt;|ne| D[getFallbackQueries diet mealType]\n    D --&gt; E[Pro každý fallback query]\n    E --&gt; F[searchMealMetadata fallbackQuery]\n    F --&gt; G{recipeVerified?}\n    G --&gt;|ano| C\n    G --&gt;|ne| H[Další fallback]\n    H --&gt; E\n    E --&gt;|všechny selhaly| I[Jídlo neověřeno]\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Změny\n\n1. **deterministicFallback.js** – exportovat funkci &#96;getFallbackMealQueries(diet, mealType)&#96;:\n   - Vstup: &#96;diet&#96; (standard/vegetarian/vegan), &#96;mealType&#96; (breakfast/lunch/dinner/snack)\n   - Výstup: pole search queries z &#96;MEAL_QUERIES[dietKey][mealType]&#96;\n   - Mapování diety: &#96;vegan&#96; → vegan, &#96;vegetarian&#96; → vegetarian, ostatní → standard\n\n2. **planOrchestrator.js – resolveMeals** – rozšířit logiku při Spoonacular miss:\n   - Když &#96;meta&#96; je &#96;null&#96; nebo &#96;recipeVerified === false&#96;:\n     - Zavolat &#96;getFallbackMealQueries(diet, m.type)&#96;\n     - Pro každý fallback query (max 5–7 pokusů) volat &#96;searchMealMetadata(fallbackQuery, null, mealSearchOpts)&#96;\n     - Při prvním úspěchu (&#96;recipeVerified&#96;) použít tento výsledek místo původního\n     - Pokud všechny fallbacky selžou, ponechat stávající chování („Jídlo (neověřeno)“)\n\n3. **Optimalizace**: Fallbacky volat sekvenčně jen pro jídla, kde původní dotaz selhal – paralelní zpracování ostatních jídel zůstane beze změny.\n\n---\n\n## Soubory k úpravě\n\n| Soubor | Změna |\n|--------|-------|\n| [lib/services/deterministicFallback.js](lib/services/deterministicFallback.js) | Přidat &#96;export function getFallbackMealQueries(diet, mealType)&#96; |\n| [lib/services/planOrchestrator.js](lib/services/planOrchestrator.js) | V &#96;resolveMeals&#96;: při &#96;!recipeVerified&#96; iterovat fallback queries a retry &#96;searchMealMetadata&#96; |\n\n---\n\n## Důležité detaily\n\n- **mealSearchOpts**: Při fallbacku použít stejné &#96;mealSearchOpts&#96; jako u původního dotazu (včetně &#96;fastMode&#96;).\n- **Retry**: Fallbacky neobalují &#96;withRetry&#96; – každý fallback je jeden pokus; při selhání jdeme na další.\n- **Limit**: Max 5–7 fallback pokusů na jídlo, aby se neprodlužovala latence.\n- **replace-meal API**: Zůstává beze změny; fallback je jen v pipeline &#96;resolveMeals&#96;.\n",

## 1. `lib/services/deterministicFallback.js`

Přidána funkce `getFallbackMealQueries(diet, mealType)`:
- Vstup: `diet` (standard/vegetarian/vegan), `mealType` (breakfast/lunch/dinner/snack)
- Výstup: pole search queries z `MEAL_QUERIES` pro danou dietu a typ jídla

## 2. `lib/services/planOrchestrator.js`

V `resolveMeals` je nová fallback logika:
- Po prvním volání Spoonacular pro každé jídlo
- Pokud `meta` je `null` nebo `recipeVerified === false`:
  - Zavolá se `getFallbackMealQueries(diet, m.type)`
  - Pro každé jídlo se zkusí až 5 fallback dotazů
  - Při prvním úspěchu se použije výsledek místo původního
- Fallbacky pro různá jídla běží paralelně (`Promise.all`)
- Pro každé jídlo se fallbacky zkouší sekvenčně
- Při selhání všech fallbacků zůstává „Jídlo (neověřeno)“

_**User**_

Jsi AI asistent osobního trenéra Ondry Nováka. Komunikuješ lidsky, přirozeně a profesionálně. Tvým cílem je pochopit situaci uživatele, dát mu hodnotu a navést ho na další krok (např. kontakt nebo upřesnění cíle).

Ondra Novák je osobní trenér a výživový poradce s 18+ lety zkušeností s pohybem a 6+ lety praxe. Zaměřuje se na hubnutí, nabírání svalů, kondici, mobilitu a celkový životní styl. Jeho přístup je individuální, bez extrémů, zaměřený na dlouhodobé výsledky a správné návyky.

Při komunikaci:
- vždy personalizuj odpověď podle cíle a zkušeností
- ptej se na kontext (cíl, zkušenosti, omezení)
- vysvětluj jednoduše a srozumitelně
- motivuj, ale netlač

Používej formulace:
- „Podle toho, co píšeš…“
- „U Ondry je výhoda, že…“
- „Důležité je, že…“
- „Aby to dávalo smysl přesně pro tebe…“

Nikdy:
- nevymýšlej ceny nebo detaily služeb
- neslibuj garantované výsledky
- nedávej lékařské rady

Vždy směřuj odpověď k tomu, aby uživatel udělal další krok.

---

_**User**_

Chovej se jako senior full-stack QA + product engineer a proveď finální verifikační audit v projektu Body & Mind ON.

Cíl:
ověřit, že produkční flow generování plánů je konzistentní, lokalizované do češtiny a že profil, e-mail i popup receptu zobrazují jen správná a ověřená data.

## Co musíš ověřit

### 1. Hlavní pipeline
Zkontroluj, že hlavní generování plánu skutečně funguje takto:
OpenAI structured input
-> Spoonacular pro jídla
-> wger pro cviky
-> localized/canonical view model
-> renderer
-> profil + e-mail

Ověř, že:
- OpenAI negeneruje finální user-facing názvy jako source of truth
- jídla jsou resolved přes Spoonacular
- cviky jsou resolved přes wger
- renderer nepouští raw angličtinu do UI

### 2. Jídla
Zkontroluj:
- `display_name_cs`
- `recipe_verified`
- `recipe_id`
- `image_trust_level`
- že obrázek jídla je použit jen při dostatečné confidence / exact trust
- že při slabém matchi se nezobrazuje chybný obrázek
- že se nikde do UI/e-mailu nepropíše raw `recipe.title`

### 3. Popup receptu
Zkontroluj:
- `/api/spoonacular-recipe`
- že title je česky
- že suroviny jsou česky
- že postup je česky
- že lokalizace používá cache / helper vrstvu a nevrací raw Spoonacular EN data

### 4. Cviky
Zkontroluj:
- `display_name_cs`
- `canonical_key`
- `exercise_verified`
- že profil a e-mail zobrazují jen `display_name_cs` nebo controlled placeholder
- že `replace-workout` už nevrací raw `resolved.name` jako user-facing text

### 5. Renderer
Zkontroluj:
- profil HTML
- e-mail HTML
- nákupní seznam
- seznam cviků

Ověř, že renderer používá pouze:
- `meal.display_name_cs`
- `exercise.display_name_cs`
- nebo controlled placeholdery:
  - `Jídlo`
  - `Jídlo (neověřeno)`
  - `Cvik`
  - `Cvik (neověřeno)`

A že už nepoužívá jako user-facing fallback:
- `recipe.title`
- `m.display_name`
- `ex.name`
- raw text z OpenAI

### 6. Replace flow
Zkontroluj:
- `pages/api/onboarding/replace-meal.js`
- `pages/api/onboarding/replace-workout.js`

Ověř, že:
- replace-meal vrací localized meal model
- replace-workout vrací `display_name_cs`, `canonical_key`, `exercise_verified`
- oba endpointy vrací stejný model jako hlavní pipeline

### 7. Poslední riziko: canonical cviky
Prověř `exerciseProviderRegistry` a související vrstvu.

Ověř:
- kdy se bere `display_name_cs` z canonical mapy
- kdy fallbackuje na raw wger name
- kdy se používá AI alternative fallback
- jestli je možné v produkci, že se uživateli zobrazí nehezký nebo neplně český název cviku mimo canonical mapu

Tohle vyhodnoť zvlášť jako:
- PASS
- RISK
- FAIL

## Co máš projít
Minimálně:
- lib/services/planOrchestrator.js
- lib/planRenderer.js
- lib/recipeLocalization.js
- pages/api/spoonacular-recipe.js
- pages/api/onboarding/replace-meal.js
- pages/api/onboarding/replace-workout.js
- lib/services/exerciseProviderRegistry.js
- lib/exerciseEnrichment.js
- email render flow
- profil flow

## Výstup chci přesně takto

### A. Celkový verdict
Jedna věta:
- HOTOVO
nebo
- HOTOVO S RIZIKEM
nebo
- NENÍ HOTOVO

### B. PASS / RISK / FAIL tabulka
Vyhodnoť samostatně:
- Spoonacular meals
- localized meal titles
- localized recipe popup
- trust-safe meal images
- wger exercises
- canonical Czech exercise names
- renderer profile
- renderer email
- replace meal
- replace workout

### C. Root causes
Seznam všeho, co ještě může způsobit:
- angličtinu v UI
- špatné obrázky
- rozdíl mezi profilem a e-mailem
- rozdíl mezi pipeline a replace endpointy

### D. Kritická místa v kódu
U každého napiš:
- soubor
- funkce
- problém
- dopad

### E. Co je už správně
Vyjmenuj věci, které jsou už v pořádku a není potřeba je znovu předělávat.

### F. Co ještě dorazit
Jen konkrétní zbytky, ne obecné rady.

### G. Testovací checklist
Sepiš finální ruční QA checklist pro produkci:
1. nová registrace
2. profil
3. e-mail
4. popup receptu
5. replace meal
6. replace workout
7. edge case s neznámým cvikem
8. edge case se slabým meal match

## Důležité pravidlo
Nevěř dokumentaci, pokud odporuje kódu.
Jako zdroj pravdy ber aktuální implementaci.
Pokud někde existuje fallback, uveď ho explicitně.
Pokud něco není 100% canonical-only, napiš to natvrdo.

---


Audit je hotový. Shrnutí:

---

## A. Celkový verdict

**HOTOVO S RIZIKEM**

---

## B. PASS / RISK / FAIL tabulka

| Oblast | Status |
|-------|--------|
| Spoonacular meals | PASS |
| localized meal titles | PASS |
| localized recipe popup | PASS |
| trust-safe meal images | PASS |
| wger exercises | PASS |
| **canonical Czech exercise names** | **RISK** |
| renderer profile | PASS |
| renderer email | PASS |
| replace meal | PASS |
| replace workout | PASS |

---

## C. Root causes

- **Angličtina v UI:** `exerciseCanonicalMap.js` má u cviků `mountain_climber`, `superman`, `bench_press` v `display_name_cs` anglické názvy.
- Ostatní body (obrázky, profil vs. e-mail, pipeline vs. replace) jsou v pořádku.

---

## D. Kritická místa v kódu

- **lib/exerciseCanonicalMap.js** – `display_name_cs` pro mountain_climber, superman, bench_press je anglicky → anglické názvy v profilu a e-mailu.

---

## E. Co je už správně

- Pipeline: OpenAI → Spoonacular → wger → localized view → renderer
- OpenAI negeneruje finální user-facing názvy
- Jídla přes Spoonacular, fallback při miss
- Překlad receptů (batchTranslateRecipeTitlesToCzech, getLocalizedRecipe)
- Renderer používá jen `display_name_cs`, `recipe_verified`, `exercise_verified`
- Obrázky jen při `image_trust_level === 'exact'`
- Replace endpointy vrací stejný model jako hlavní pipeline
- Cviky mimo canonical mapu → placeholder „Cvik“, nikdy raw wger name

---

## F. Co ještě dorazit

1. **exerciseCanonicalMap.js** – doplnit české `display_name_cs` pro mountain_climber, superman, bench_press (např. „Horolezec“, „Superman cvik“, „Tlak na lavici“).

---

## G. Testovací checklist

V dokumentu je 8 kroků ruční QA: nová registrace, profil, e-mail, popup receptu, replace meal, replace workout, neznámý cvik, slabý meal match.

---

Celá zpráva je v souboru `docs/AUDIT_VERIFICATION_PRODUCTION_2026.md`.

---

_**User**_

dej to do pprodukce a zzapracuj bod F. 

---

_**Agent (model composer-2, mode Agent)**_

Hotovo. Zrychlil jsem generování plánu při registraci:

### Změny

1. **Méně fallbacků při registraci** (`planOrchestrator.js`)
   - Při `initial_plan` (registrace) se místo 5 pokusů o fallback jídla používá jen **1**
   - U neověřených jídel se rychleji přechází na „Jídlo (neověřeno)“ místo opakovaných volání Spoonacular

2. **Kratší timeout pro Spoonacular** (`mealEnrichment.js`)
   - V režimu registrace: **3 s** místo 5 s na jedno volání
   - Pomalé odpovědi Spoonacular se dříve přeruší a pokračuje se dál

### Dopad

- **Předtím:** až 5 × Spoonacular volání na každé neověřené jídlo (21 jídel → až 105 volání)
- **Teď:** max 1 fallback na jídlo, timeout 3 s → výrazně méně čekání

### Nasazení

- Commit `22916b4` je pushnutý na `main`
- Vercel nasadí novou verzi automaticky

Registrace by teď měla proběhnout výrazně rychleji. Pokud to stále trvá dlouho, může jít o:
- pomalý OpenAI (strukturovaný plán),
- pomalý Spoonacular,
- nebo Vercel limit 60 s (Hobby plan).

Shrnutí analýzy:

---

## Proč je tolik Spoonacular požadavků

### 1. **Dvojité volání pro stejná jídla**

- **Generování plánu** (planOrchestrator): 21 jídel → 21× `complexSearch` (cca 6 bodů/call ≈ 126 bodů)
- **Zobrazení profilu** (plan-enrichment): PlanViewer při načtení plánu volá `/api/plan-enrichment` → znovu 21× Spoonacular

**Příčina:** planOrchestrator volá `searchMealMetadata` přímo a **nezapisuje do `meal_metadata_cache`**. plan-enrichment pak nemá cache hit a znovu volá Spoonacular pro stejná jídla.

### 2. **Drahé endpointy**

- `complexSearch` s `addRecipeInformation=true` a `addRecipeNutrition=true` ≈ **6 bodů** za volání (3 request + 1/result)
- Get Recipe Information (popup receptu) ≈ **1 bod** za otevření

### 3. **Kdy se volá Spoonacular**

| Událost | Odhad bodů |
|---------|------------|
| 1 registrace (plán + první profil) | ~250–380 |
| Přegenerování plánu | ~250 |
| Zobrazení profilu (cache miss) | ~126 |
| Otevření receptu v modalu | 1 |

### 4. **Kritická místa v kódu**

- `lib/services/planOrchestrator.js` – `resolveMeals` volá `searchMealMetadata` bez zápisu do cache
- `lib/enrichPlanContent.js` – `enrichMeal` pro každé jídlo, při cache miss → Spoonacular
- `components/PlanViewer.js` – při každém načtení plánu volá `/api/plan-enrichment`

---

## Doporučené úpravy

1. **P1:** V `planOrchestrator.resolveMeals` po úspěšném `searchMealMetadata` volat `setCachedMeal` (nebo ekvivalent) a ukládat výsledky včetně `recipe_id`, aby `getCachedMealByRecipeId` v plan-enrichment mohl najít data bez volání Spoonacular.
2. **P2:** Ukládat cache i pod klíčem `recipe:{id}`, aby lookup podle `recipe_id` byl spolehlivý.
3. **P3:** V PlanViewer cachovat odpověď Get Recipe Information podle `recipeId`, aby se při opětovném otevření stejného receptu nevolalo API.

---

Detailní rozbor je v souboru `docs/SPOONACULAR_REQUEST_ANALYSIS.md`. Můžu navrhnout konkrétní změny v kódu pro P1–P3.

Shrnutí změn:

---

## Provedené změny

### P1 + P2: Cache Spoonacular z planOrchestrator

- **`lib/mealEnrichment.js`** – nová funkce `cacheMealFromPlanResult(meta, displayNameCs)` zapisuje ověřená jídla do `meal_metadata_cache` pod klíčem `recipe_{id}`.
- **`lib/services/planOrchestrator.js`** – po úspěšném resolve jídla volá `cacheMealFromPlanResult`, aby plan-enrichment mohl použít cache místo opětovného volání Spoonacular.

**Dopad:** Při zobrazení profilu s plánem se data berou z cache, ne znovu ze Spoonacular → méně requestů.

### Denní návyky: aktuální den vždy viditelný

- **`components/HabitTracker.js`** – pořadí sloupců změněno tak, aby **dnešek byl první** (dnes, zítra, pozítří, včera, …).
- Graf pod tabulkou používá chronologické pořadí (`daysChronological`).

**Dopad:** Sloupec „Dnes“ je vždy vlevo a dostupný bez scrollování.

---

## Ověření jídel a obrázků

- Jídla se zobrazují jen s ověřeným názvem (`display_name_cs`) nebo placeholderem „Jídlo (neověřeno)“.
- Obrázek se zobrazuje jen při `image_trust_level === 'exact'` (confidence ≥ 0.75 a Spoonacular vrací obrázek).
- „Bez ověřeného obrázku“ znamená, že Spoonacular nenašel dostatečně spolehlivý match s obrázkem. Díky P1/P2 se při zobrazení profilu už nepřepisují data novým voláním Spoonacular – použijí se data z cache z generování plánu.

---

## P3

- Client-side cache pro `/api/spoonacular-recipe` už v PlanViewer existuje (Map, TTL 5 min).

---

### Změny

2. **`pages/api/plan-enrichment.js`** – odstraněna in-memory cache (5 min TTL). Každé volání znovu načte data ze Spoonacular/wger.

Úpravy jsou hotové. Při zobrazení profilu se už Spoonacular nevolá.

### Změny

1. **`lib/planRenderer.js`** – do HTML plánu se při generování zapisují `data-image-url` a `data-image-trust-level` pro každé jídlo.

2. **`lib/enrichPlanContent.js`** – při zobrazení profilu:
   - parsuje `image_url` a `image_trust_level` z HTML,
   - **nepoužívá** `enrichMeal` ani Spoonacular,
   - sestavuje `meal_images` a `meal_trust` jen z dat v HTML.

### Výsledek

- **Při generování plánu** – Spoonacular se volá jen v `planOrchestrator` (21×).
- **Při zobrazení profilu** – žádné volání Spoonacular, data se berou z HTML.
- **Při změně plánu** (Nahradit jiným) – Spoonacular se volá jen v `replace-meal`.

Plán zůstává stejný, dokud ho uživatel sám nezmění.
